note: A school-based sample of healthy Greek adolescents studied for anthropometric and pubertal traits; despite 'Genes and Environment' in its name, dietary data are collected among many variables with no exposure stated as the design purpose, and the participants are healthy.

label: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
quote: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) is a panel study of a representative cohort of men and women living in England aged ≥50 years.
note: A representative panel study of ageing in adults aged 50 and over in England, multidisciplinary in scope; neither exposure-defined nor about one disease.

label: The Fenland Study
quote: The Fenland study is designed to investigate the interaction between genetic and lifestyle factors in determining diabetes, obesity, and related metabolic disorders.
note: A population-based Cambridgeshire cohort whose stated design is the interaction of genetic and lifestyle factors in diabetes, obesity and related metabolic disorders: lifestyle exposure is a stated design purpose (the bundle shows habitual diet measured; the source names only 'lifestyle factors'), and the outcome is one disease family, so it is a population study of metabolic disease.

label: The Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren
quote: HGF-Study The HGF GWA study (center 1: Wichmann, Sauter, center 2: Bickeböller, Rosenberger, center 3: Risch, Chang-Claude) was made up of three independent German studies as detailed below: In total 506 incident lung cancer cases (LUCY-study: n=305, Heidelberg lung cancer case-control study: n=201) were compared to 480 popula-tion controls (KORA surveys KORA).
note: The catalogue tag denotes the Helmholtz (HGF) lung cancer GWAS, a German lung cancer case-control collection (LUCY and Heidelberg cases against KORA population controls), so it is classified as a lung cancer patient cohort; the COHO definition instead describes the research organisation, and no exposure defines the sample.

label: The MANOLIS cohort
quote: Here, we perform whole-genome-sequence-based association analysis between 257 cardiometabolic disease-related serum protein levels9 and 13,419,876 single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in a population-based cohort (MANOLIS), and assess colocalization, causation and predictive power of protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) in cardiometabolic disease.
note: A population-based isolate cohort from the Mylopotamos villages of Crete used for genetic association with cardiometabolic and other complex traits; neither exposure-defined nor selected for a disease.

label: The Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset
quote: The individual GWAS data sets from Iceland and the Netherlands were adjusted for genomic inflation before inclusion in the meta-analysis.
note: The Dutch data set is one of the six abdominal aortic aneurysm GWAS data sets (4972 AAA cases in all, with Rotterdam Study controls) in the AAA meta-analysis, so it is an AAA case-control collection; its own composition is given only in an online table, hence medium confidence, and nothing suggests an exposure basis.

label: The Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma
quote: The Swedish/Norwegian GWAS5 was based on 1,668 and 157 MM patients from the Swedish National Myeloma Biobank (Skåne University Hospital, Lund, Sweden) and the Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma (Trondheim, Norway), respectively.
note: A biobank of multiple myeloma patients in Trondheim providing cases for myeloma susceptibility GWAS; no exposure basis.

label: The Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study
quote: By March 2009, PROMIS had recruited over 5,000 cases of first-ever confirmed acute myocardial infarction (MI) and over 5,000 matched controls aged 30-80 years.
note: A Pakistani case-control study of first acute myocardial infarction with matched controls; lifestyle is recorded as one class of determinant among genetic and biochemical ones, not as the design's exposure focus.

label: The Secondary Manifestations of ARTerial disease study
quote: The Second Manifestations of ARTerial disease (SMART) study is a single-centre prospective cohort study among patients, newly referred to the hospital with (1) clinically manifest atherosclerotic vessel disease, or (2) marked risk factors for atherosclerosis.
note: A hospital cohort of patients referred with manifest atherosclerotic vascular disease (or marked atherosclerosis risk factors, an at-risk minority) followed for cardiovascular events; disease-based recruitment, no exposure basis.

label: The Hellenic study of Interactions between Single nucleotide polymorphisms and Eating in Atherosclerosis Susceptibility
quote: The sample under study comprised 924 Greek individuals (390 cases with CAD and 534 controls) from the THISEAS study.
note: A Greek coronary artery disease case-control collection, so a disease cohort of CAD patients; the exposure verdict rests on the study's name alone, which states its subject as interactions between SNPs and eating in atherosclerosis susceptibility, since the bundled papers use it only as a CAD case-control set and describe no dietary design.

label: Treating to New Targets
quote: A total of 10,001 patients with clinically evident CHD and LDL cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) were randomly assigned to double-blind therapy and received either 10 mg or 80 mg of atorvastatin per day.
note: A randomised statin trial in patients with clinically evident stable coronary heart disease; the intervention is a medication, not an exposure.

label: Twins Early Development Study
quote: The Twins Early Development Study (TEDS) is a longitudinal twin study that recruited over 16,000 twin-pairs born between 1994 and 1996 in England and Wales through national birth records.
note: A population twin birth cohort recruited from national birth records to study cognitive, behavioural and emotional development; an EGA subset was screened for autism, but the cohort itself is neither exposure-defined nor about one disease.

label: Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium
quote: The Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium (T1DGC) is an international project whose primary aims are to: (a) discover genes that modify type 1 diabetes risk; and (b) expand upon the existing genetic resources for type 1 diabetes research. The initial goal was to collect 2500 affected sibling pair (ASP) families worldwide.
note: A consortium collecting affected sib-pair families, trios, cases and controls for type 1 diabetes genetics, so an aggregation of type 1 diabetes patient collections; no exposure basis.

label: UK Adult Twin Register
quote: The UK Adult Twin Registry (or TwinsUK Registry) is a cohort of volunteer adult twins from all over the United Kingdom.
note: A registry of volunteer adult twins studied for ageing and complex disorders in general; a twin registry with a broad remit, so neither an exposure nor a disease cohort.

label: UK Biobank
quote: As described in the manuscript, the MRC and Wellcome Trust played a key role in the decision to establish UK Biobank, a large, population-based, prospective, open access resource that would allow detailed investigations of the genetic and environmental determinants of the diseases of middle and old age.
note: A population-based biobank of half a million UK adults for the genetic and environmental determinants of diseases of middle and old age in general; environmental determinants are mentioned as one broad class among many and the disease remit is broad, so no on both counts despite its listing in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue.

label: UK Brain Expression Consortium
quote: Central nervous system (CNS) tissues originating from 134 control individuals was collected by the Medical Research Council (MRC) Sudden Death Brain and Tissue Bank, Edinburgh, UK (Millar et al. 2007), and the Sun Health Research Institute (SHRI) an affiliate of Sun Health Corporation, USA (Beach et al. 2008).
note: A consortium of post-mortem brain tissue from neuropathologically normal control donors used for expression QTL mapping; donors were selected as neurologically healthy, so neither an exposure nor a disease cohort.

label: UK Childhood Cancer Study
quote: An investigation into the possible causes of childhood cancer has been carried out throughout England, Scotland and Wales over the period 1991-1998. All children known to be suffering from one or other type of the disease over periods of 4-5 years have been included, and control children matched for sex, age and area of residence have been selected at random from population registers.
note: A national case-control study of all children with cancer in Great Britain 1991-1998 and matched population controls, set up to find the causes of childhood cancer with measurement of radon, gamma radiation and electromagnetic field exposure built into its design; so a cancer patient cohort that is also designed to study exposures.

label: UK Household Longitudinal Study
quote: The UKHLS is a longitudinal survey of the members of approximately 40,000 households in the UK
note: Understanding Society is a general household panel survey of the UK population covering education, employment, income, health and family life; it selects on neither an exposure nor a disease and served as general population controls.

label: UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium
diseases: inflammatory bowel disease | Crohn's disease | ulcerative colitis
quote: With the support of Crohn’s and Colitis UK, the UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium has been at the front of this research – building a vast database of genetic and clinical data from patients across the UK.
note: A consortium of UK inflammatory bowel disease patient collections (Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis cases) assembled for genetic studies; no environmental exposure defines it.

label: Viking Health Study
quote: The Viking Health Study—Shetland (hereafter VIKING1) is a geographically defined cohort with grandparents from the Shetland Isles, north of Scotland, which seeks to identify genetic factors influencing cardiovascular and other disease risk54.
note: A population-isolate genetic cohort of Shetland volunteers with a broad remit (risk factors for common diseases such as heart disease, diabetes, glaucoma and stroke); not selected by exposure or by any one disease.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
diseases: bipolar disorder | coronary artery disease | Crohn's disease | hypertension | rheumatoid arthritis | type 1 diabetes | type 2 diabetes | ankylosing spondylitis | autoimmune thyroid disease | breast cancer | inflammatory bowel disease | multiple sclerosis | tuberculosis | Parkinson's disease
quote: We describe a joint GWA study (using the Affymetrix GeneChip 500K Mapping Array Set) undertaken in the British population, which has examined approximately 2,000 individuals for each of 7 major diseases and a shared set of approximately 3,000 controls.
note: A consortium of disease-specific case collections (seven common diseases in the 2007 study, further diseases in the member case-control studies) with shared population controls; classified by the patient collections it aggregates, with no exposure basis.

label: Basquecolon cohort
quote: Basque-colon cohort included 873 participants with colon cancer, biobanked between 2009- 2019. Participants were diagnosed and/or treated according to usual clinical practice in the Donostia University Hospital, San Sebastian, Spain, including follow-up to this date.
note: A hospital case series of colon cancer patients (with comparison participants) used as a colorectal cancer PRS validation set; no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: The cohort's own description names colon cancer patients from Donostia University Hospital; colorectal cancer is the paper's broader subject, not the cohort's recruitment basis, so naming it too is too broad.

label: INTERVAL study
quote: INTERVAL is a randomised trial of whole blood donors enrolled from all 25 static centres of NHS Blood and Transplant.
note: A randomised trial of healthy whole-blood donors comparing donation intervals; the intervention is a procedure, not an environmental exposure, and donors have no disease.

label: CONVERGE
quote: Here, using low-coverage whole-genome sequencing of 5,303 Chinese women with recurrent MDD selected to reduce phenotypic heterogeneity, and 5,337 controls screened to exclude MDD, we identified, and subsequently replicated in an independent sample, two loci contributing to risk of MDD on chromosome 10
note: A case-control collection of Han Chinese women with recurrent major depressive disorder and screened controls; no exposure basis.

label: Gene-Environmental Interaction and phenotype study
quote: In this study, we used data from the Gene-Environment of Interaction and phenotype (GENIE) cohort, and the Health and Prevention Enhancement (H-PEACE) cohort, at the Seoul National University Hospital Healthcare System Gangnam Center, where comprehensive health check-ups and screening are done in Korean populations.
note: A health check-up biobank cohort of Korean examinees; despite the gene-environment name, the paper describes deep clinical phenotyping with environment and lifestyle mentioned only generically, not a design built around measuring environmental exposures, and no disease selection.

label: China Atherosclerosis Study
quote: CAS consisted of 1,010 cases of CAD and 3,998 controls. 1,010 cases from the Northern provinces in China were enrolled from Fuwai Hospital, National Center of Cardiovascular Diseases. 83.8% of cases have a family history of CAD.
note: A Han Chinese case-control collection of hospital-enrolled coronary artery disease cases and population controls; no exposure basis.

label: Diabetes Prediction and Prevention
quote: The carriers of the genotype DQB1*02/DQB1*03:02 or DQB1*03:02/x genotypes (here x≠ DQB1*02, DQB1*03:01, DQB1*06:02, or DQB1*06:03 alleles) were categorized into the T1D risk group and recruited for the DIPP follow up program.
note: A Finnish birth cohort in which newborns carrying HLA genotypes conferring type 1 diabetes risk are followed for islet autoimmunity and diabetes; selection is by genetic risk, not by exposure.

label: Functional genomic diagnostic tools for coronary artery disease
quote: This study investigated the association of clinical, demographic, and genetic factors with severe coronary artery stenosis phenotypes in our population composed of 1734 individuals with severe coronary stenosis (≥ 50% in coronary vessels) and comparing them to 757 controls with no evidence of stenosis on angiography.
note: A Lebanese series of patients undergoing coronary angiography, analysed as severe coronary stenosis cases against angiographic controls; a clinical disease cohort with no exposure basis.

label: German Chronic Kidney Disease Study
quote: The German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study is a prospective observational national cohort study. It aims to enrol a total of 5000 patients with CKD of various aetiologies, who are under nephrological care, and to follow them for up to 10 years.
note: A prospective cohort of chronic kidney disease patients under nephrological care in Germany; no exposure basis.

label: German Longevity Study
quote: The examined sample comprised 1351 German LLI (≥94 years, including 643 centenarians) and 4680 German younger controls.
note: Long-lived individuals (94 years and older) compared with younger controls: selection is by the trait of longevity, which is out of scope as a disease, and there is no exposure basis.

label: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
quote: GRACE (the Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events) is a large, prospective, multinational observational study of patients hospitalized with ACS.
note: A multinational registry of patients hospitalised with acute coronary syndromes; no exposure basis.

label: TwinGene Study
quote: TwinGene is a cross-sectional study where participants underwent a health examination and venous blood sample collection at a local health care facility between 2004 and 2008.
note: A twin-registry sub-study in which Swedish twins had a health examination and blood draw; twin registries are unselected on exposure and disease.

label: Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men
quote: ULSAM started as a health investigation, focused at identifying metabolic risk factors for cardiovascular disease, to which all 50 year-old men living in Uppsala in 1970 were invited.
note: A population cohort of all 50-year-old men in Uppsala set up to identify metabolic risk factors for cardiovascular disease (later broadened to ageing); diet and physical activity are measured among many variables, so no exposure design.

label: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Ageing
quote: The National Institute on Aging’s Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) is America's longest-running scientific study of human aging.
note: A longitudinal study of normal human ageing in healthy volunteers; ageing is not a disease and there is no exposure basis.

label: Motor Neuron Disease Biobank study
quote: Adults attending one of 20 UK hospitals and who had been diagnosed with ALS by two consultant neurologists were invited to participate in the UK National DNA Bank for Motor Neuron Disease Research (MND DNA bank), a national collection of ALS DNA samples derived from whole blood.
note: A national DNA bank of patients diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at UK hospitals; no exposure basis.

label: Singapore Diabetic Cohort Study
quote: The diabetic cohort (DC) was set up to study the determinants of complications in individuals with type 2 diabetes and examine the role of genetic, physiological and lifestyle factors in the development of complications in these individuals.
note: A cohort of adults with physician-diagnosed type 2 diabetes recruited from Singapore clinics to study complications; lifestyle is one factor among many, not an exposure design.

label: Ely Study
quote: The Ely study, established in 1990, is a prospective study of the etiology of type 2 diabetes, as described in detail elsewhere (18, 19).
note: A population-based cohort of non-diabetic adults from one Ely practice followed to study the incidence and aetiology of type 2 diabetes; no exposure basis.

label: Genetic Asthma Susceptibility to Indoor Pollution in Peru
quote: A total of 436 Peruvian children (aged 9-19 years) with asthma and 291 without asthma were genotyped by using the Illumina Multi-Ethnic Global Array.
note: A case-control study of Peruvian children with and without asthma built, as its name states, to study genetic susceptibility to indoor pollution (the paper describes it as evaluating genetics, environment and asthma status); the pollution design is stated only through the study's name, so the exposure verdict is medium.

label: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative
quote: The Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) is an observational, international study designed to establish biomarker-defined cohorts and identify clinical, imaging, genetic, and biospecimen Parkinson's disease (PD) progression markers to accelerate disease-modifying therapeutic trials.
note: An international biomarker cohort of untreated early Parkinson's disease patients (with healthy controls and SWEDD subjects) followed for progression markers; no exposure basis.

label: Psychosis Endophenotype Consortium
diseases: psychosis | schizophrenia | schizoaffective disorder | psychotic bipolar disorder
quote: 1239 cases with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or psychotic bipolar disorder; 857 of their unaffected relatives, and 2739 healthy controls were genotyped with the Affymetrix 6.0 single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array.
note: A consortium of psychosis case collections (schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, psychotic bipolar disorder) with their unaffected relatives and controls; classified by the patient collections it aggregates, with no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: The record stands: a consortium of psychosis cases (schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, psychotic bipolar disorder) with relatives and controls, and the quote is verbatim. Only the mapping of psychotic bipolar disorder to bipolar disorder is too broad.

label: Study of Health in Pomerania
quote: A sample of 7008 women and men aged 20 to 79 years in a north-east region of Germany, 4900 expected participants. The sample was drawn in two steps: First, 32 communities in the region were selected. Second, within the communities a simple random sample was drawn from residence registries, stratified by gender and age.
note: Population-based random samples of adults in West Pomerania examined for a broad range of diseases and risk factors; neither an exposure nor a single disease defines the SHIP cohorts.

label: The Cooperative Health Research in South Tyrol
quote: The Cooperative Health Research In South Tyrol (CHRIS) study is a population-based study with a longitudinal lookout to investigate the genetic and molecular basis of age-related common chronic conditions and their interaction with life style and environment in the general population.
note: A general-population study of the Vinschgau valley with a broad remit of age-related chronic conditions; lifestyle and environment are mentioned as interacting factors, not as an exposure-centred design, and no single disease defines it.

label: The Health Effects of Arsenic Longitudinal Study
quote: In the prospective cohort Health Effects of Arsenic Longitudinal Study (HEALS), trained physicians unaware of arsenic exposure interviewed in person and clinically assessed 11 746 population-based participants (aged 18-75 years) from Araihazar, Bangladesh.
note: Population-based prospective cohort of adults in an arsenic-affected rural area of Bangladesh, set up to study the health effects of arsenic in drinking water; the outcomes are all-cause and chronic-disease mortality broadly, not one disease.

label: 100,000 Genomes Project
quote: In a pilot study for the 100,000 Genomes Project, we generated WGS data for 13,037 participants, of whom 9,802 had a rare disease, and provided a genetic diagnosis to 1,138 of the 7,065 patients with detailed phenotypic data.
note: NHS patients with rare diseases or cancer, and their relatives, sequenced by Genomics England for diagnosis; the quoted pilot describes the rare disease arm and the cancer arm comes from the definition. No exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: The only source on disk (the EGA study page, read in full with cached.py) describes rare disease patients only and never mentions cancer; the cancer arm rests on the COHO definition alone, so it is dropped until a source is quoted. The rare disease verdict and verbatim quote stand.

label: 1958 British Birth Cohort
quote: The 1958 National Child Development Study (NCDS) is following the lives of an initial 17,415 people born in England, Scotland and Wales in a single week of 1958.
note: General birth cohort of everyone born in Great Britain in one week of March 1958, followed for health, cognition and social outcomes and used as population controls; no exposure or disease selection.

label: 300BCG
quote: To investigate human population variation of trained immunity, we immunized healthy individuals with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG).
note: Healthy volunteers vaccinated with BCG to study variation in trained immunity; vaccination is an intervention, not an environmental exposure, and the participants are healthy.

label: AACR Project GENIE
quote: Methods: This retrospective cohort study analysed genomics data for 121,771 patients who had undergone targeted sequencing compiled by the Genomics Evidence Neoplasia Information Exchange (GENIE) or Foundation Medicine (FM). A statistical approach was developed to identify patients with GCV-associated mutational signature (GCVsig) from targeted sequenced data of tumour samples.
note: AACR registry aggregating clinical tumour sequencing and outcomes of cancer patients from participating cancer centres; the EGA study used it as a cohort of 121,771 sequenced tumour samples. No exposure basis.

label: AC-ANGIOPREDICT Phase II trial
quote: Low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (LC-WGS) was performed on tumor tissue, normal tissue and plasma samples collected from mCRC patients from the AC-ANGIOPREDICT Phase II trial (NCT01822444) and the University Medical Center Mannheim (UMM).
note: Phase II trial cohort of metastatic colorectal cancer patients treated with bevacizumab-containing therapy; treatment is a medication, not an environmental exposure. Checked 2026-09-25: A phase II trial of metastatic colorectal cancer patients; verdict, role and verbatim quote stand, but the mapped term is broader than the disease the source names.

label: Adjuvant Lapatinib and/or Trastuzumab Treatment Optimisation trial
quote: Here, by performing gene expression profiling in HER2-positive breast cancers from patients receiving adjuvant trastuzumab in the ALTTO clinical trial, we identified and characterized five molecular subtypes associated with the risk of distant recurrence
note: Phase III adjuvant trial cohort of women with HER2-positive early breast cancer; no exposure basis.

label: African Collaborative Center for Microbiome and Genomics Research
diseases: cervical cancer | persistent high-risk HPV infection
quote: The design of the African Collaborative Center for Microbiome and Genomics Research (ACCME) HPV and Cervical Cancer Cohort Study enables us to study environmental, microbiomic, genetic and epigenetic factors associated with persistent hrHPV infection, in order to improve knowledge of the mechanism of HPV carcinogenesis and discover biomarkers of persistent hrHPV infection and cervical cancer.
note: HIV-negative women from the general population of Abuja enrolled in a cohort set up to study persistent hrHPV infection and cervical cancer; they were not selected for an environmental exposure, and smoking and other risk factors are measured only as covariates. Checked 2026-09-25: A cohort of HIV-negative women from the general population of Abuja set up to study persistent hrHPV infection and cervical cancer; the verdict and verbatim quote stand, but HPV infection in general is broader than the persistent high-risk infection the source names.

label: African Genome Resource
quote: Whole genome DNAseq data at 4x-8x depth from approximately 3,000 Africans of 14 distinct ethnicities
note: A genome reference resource (haplotype reference panel, transcriptomes and an informatics centre) built from African population samples of many ethnicities; no exposure or disease basis.

label: African Genome Variation Project
quote: The African Genome Variation Project represents dense genotypes from 1,481 individuals and whole-genome sequences from 320 individuals across sub-Saharan Africa.
note: Population-genetic resource of individuals from 18 ethno-linguistic groups across sub-Saharan Africa, assembled to characterise genetic diversity; no exposure or disease selection.

label: African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research
note: Consortium that brings together population cohorts, genome resources and diabetes case collections from sub-Saharan Africa to study the genetics of chronic disease broadly; a broad chronic-disease purpose is not a disease cohort, and nothing in it is exposure-based.

label: ALLG ALL06
quote: ALL06 clinical trial described the efficacy and tolerability of AYA ALL patients aged 15-39 years treated on a single minimal residual disease (MRD)-stratified platform.
note: Adolescent and young adult patients with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia treated on the ALLG ALL06 protocol; no exposure basis.

label: Alpe-DPD study
quote: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) with patients treated with fluoropyrimidines was performed to identify genetic variants linked to the severe fluoropyrimidine-related toxicity.
note: Adult cancer patients starting fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy in Dutch hospitals, genotyped for DPYD variants and toxicity; the EGA text names only the treatment and the definition names cancer. Drug treatment is not an environmental exposure.

label: APCDR Diabetes Case Control Study
quote: Collection of type 2 diabetes cases of Zulu descent for studies of the genetic basis of diabetes in African populations.
note: Collection of type 2 diabetes cases of Zulu descent assembled by APCDR for diabetes genetics; no exposure basis.

label: Atlas of Blood Cancer Genomes
diseases: blood cancer | blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
quote: To address this gap, we performed integrated DNA and RNA sequencing on 88 BPDCN patients representing the largest and most ancestrally diverse cohort described to date (~77% European, ~16% Asian, ~7% African).
note: Project assembling and sequencing cohorts of patients with distinct blood cancers (BPDCN, high-grade B-cell lymphoma, T lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma) into a genomic atlas; the quoted EGA study is its BPDCN cohort. No exposure basis.

label: Australian childhood AML cohort
quote: The prevalence of extremely rare variants in the combined childhood AML cohort (n=72) was compared to that in the Medical Genome Reference Bank (MGRB; n=2570) comprising individuals aged at least 70 years with no history of cardiovascular disease, dementia or cancer.
note: Australian children with acute myeloid leukaemia whose exomes were screened for germline cancer-predisposition variants; no exposure basis.

label: BEACON eczema drug trial
quote: Defining the spatial transcriptome and cell-cell interactions in atopic dermatitis skin
note: Patients with atopic dermatitis enrolled in the BEACON eczema drug trial, profiled for the Human Cell Atlas; the EGA page gives only a title-level statement of the disease. No exposure basis.

label: Beat AML
quote: Within the beatAML cohort 39 , a bone marrow sample and a paired skin sample were taken from 261 AML patients.
note: Acute myeloid leukaemia patients of the Beat AML programme whose tumour specimens were sequenced and drug-tested; chemotherapy in the secondary analysis is treatment, not an environmental exposure.

label: Belgian Approach of Local Laboratory Extensive Tumor Testing
quote: This 2-year study involves the consortium of 9 cooperating Belgian NGS laboratories and will enroll 936 metastatic or locally advanced cancer patients coming from 13 different Belgian hospitals and cancer centers.
note: Belgian precision-oncology study enrolling metastatic or locally advanced cancer patients for comprehensive genomic profiling; no exposure basis.

label: BELLINI trial
quote: Single-cell RNA-Seq data and TCR sequencing data (both by 10X Genomics) of 51 TNBC primary tumors obtained from 29 unique patients from BELLINI clinical trial.
note: Phase 2 trial cohort of patients with early-stage triple negative breast cancer given neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without ipilimumab; no exposure basis.

label: Blood First Assay Screening Trial
quote: BFAST is a global, open-label, multicohort trial that evaluates the efficacy and safety of multiple therapies in patients with advanced/metastatic NSCLC and targetable alterations, identified by blood-based molecular testing.
note: Multicohort trial of patients with advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer selected by blood-based molecular testing; no exposure basis.

label: Born in Bradford
quote: Born in Bradford (BiB) is similarly focused on a particular local area, the city of Bradford in the north of England, and recruited 13,858 babies between 2007 and 2011, of whom ~41% self-report as white British and ~59% as other ethnicities, predominantly Pakistani.
note: Multi-ethnic birth cohort recruited from routine maternity care in Bradford to study the determinants of childhood health broadly; it sits in the exposome catalogue but is not designed around an exposure and is not selected for a disease.

label: CALGB 40601
quote: Here, we investigated the complexity of B and T cell receptor (BCR and TCR) repertoires, reflecting antigen-specific immune response, in the context of two phase III trials, namely NeoALTTO and CALGB 40601, evaluating neoadjuvant paclitaxel with trastuzumab and/or lapatinib in women affected by HER2-positive breast cancer.
note: Phase III neoadjuvant trial cohort of women with HER2-positive breast cancer; no exposure basis.

label: Cambridge Biorepository for Translational Medicine
quote: This project involves a genotyping dataset generated using the UK Biobank Axiom™ Array Kit from donor samples provided by the Cambridge Biorepository for Translational Medicine (CBTM).
note: Biorepository of tissue and blood from organ and tissue donors in Cambridge, genotyped for Human Cell Atlas work; unselected donors with no exposure or disease basis.

label: Canadian Airways Research Group
diseases: idiopathic subglottic stenosis | trauma-induced subglottic stenosis
quote: In this study, we prospectively enrolled patients with iSGS, trauma-induced subglottic stenosis, and controls to investigate the clinical, transcriptional, and genetic features that may be associated with disease pathogenesis and treatment outcomes.
note: Prospective cohort of patients with idiopathic or trauma-induced subglottic stenosis plus controls, enrolled by the Canadian Airways Research Group; the trauma is a medical (airway) injury, not an environmental exposure. Checked 2026-09-25: The verdict, role, diseases and quote stand; the second disease is mapped to subglottic stenosis of any cause, which is broader than the trauma-induced stenosis the source names.

label: Canadian Prostate Cancer Genome Network
quote: Over 5 years, CPC-GENE will sequence the genomes of 350 intermediate risk prostate cancers to identify genetic signatures that differ in cancers that responded well to treatment compared with those that did not.
note: Men with intermediate-risk prostate cancer whose tumour genomes were sequenced by CPC-GENE; a tumour series of patients with no environmental exposure in its design.

label: Cancer Genomics of the Kidney
quote: The aim of CAGEKID is to carry out comprehensive detection of DNA markers for conventional (clear cell) renal carcinoma.
note: Tumour and constitutional DNA pairs from patients with clear cell renal carcinoma assembled by the ICGC CAGEKID project; a patient series, not an exposure cohort.

label: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands cohort
quote: To address these limitations, we analysed faecal gut microbiota from two Dutch cohorts, CeDNN (128 treated CeD patients (tCeD), 106 controls) and the Lifelines Dutch Microbiome Project (24 self-reported tCeD, 654 controls), using shotgun metagenomic sequencing.

label: CENet Cohort

note: A mega-biobank of United States military veterans enrolled through VA health care to study genetic influences on health and disease broadly. Every participant is a veteran, which the guidance counts as a war-or-military exposure basis, but the cached sources give no exposure-focused design purpose and the cohort is not built around a deployment, so the exposure verdict is borderline. No single disease: a general biobank.

label: Chinese Imaging Genetics study
quote: This study prospectively collected genomic, neuroimaging, environmental, and behavioral data from more than 7000 healthy Chinese Han participants aged 18-30 years.
note: A neuroimaging genetics cohort of healthy young Chinese Han adults whose stated aim is genetic and environmental factors and their interactions on brain phenotypes, with lifelong macro-environmental exposures (climate, air pollution, urbanization, population density, green space) derived from remote sensing and survey data for each participant's residences. Environment is half of the design, so an exposure cohort of medium confidence; healthy volunteers, so not a disease cohort.

label: African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension
quote: Participants include African-American men and women aged 18 to 70 yr who have hypertensive kidney disease and GFR between 20 and 65 ml/min per 1.73 m(2).
note: African American adults with hypertensive chronic kidney disease enrolled in a randomized trial of antihypertensive regimens and blood-pressure goals, then followed in a cohort study of kidney disease progression. Patients with the disease; drug treatment is not an environmental exposure.

label: Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
diseases: dementia | Alzheimer's disease | mild cognitive impairment
quote: The ADC started collecting samples in the year 2000 and is an ongoing, observational follow-up study of patients who visited the memory clinic of the Alzheimer Center at Amsterdam UMC, location VU University medical center (VUmc).
note: All patients who visited the memory clinic of the Alzheimer Center Amsterdam since 2000, followed for research on early diagnosis, heterogeneity and vascular factors in dementia. A memory-clinic patient series; no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: A memory-clinic patient cohort (quote verified verbatim in the cached full text), whose sample includes MCI and dementia patients and AD subgroups; only the MCI mapping is too broad.

label: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits Study
quote: The purpose of this study is to understand the role of brain proteins and neurotransmitters in the symptoms of PD compared to healthy aging.
note: A Washington University movement-disorders study following people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls with imaging, motor and cognitive testing to relate brain proteins and neurotransmitters to PD symptoms. A disease cohort with controls; no exposure basis.

label: Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease Study
quote: The purpose of this study is to understand the relationship between clinical symptoms and brain changes in people with PD as compared to healthy aging.
note: A Washington University movement-disorders study following people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls with MRI, PET and clinical testing. A disease cohort with controls; no exposure basis.

label: BioBank Japan
quote: The BBJ is a registry of patients diagnosed with any of 47 target common diseases.
note: A patient-based biobank: every participant was enrolled at a hospital as a patient with one of 47 (later 51) target common diseases, which the source contrasts with population-based biobanks. Participants are selected for having a disease, so 'patients', but the disease list is broad (cancers, cardiometabolic, respiratory and other diseases), which puts it close to the broad-purpose exclusion; no exposure basis.

label: Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study
quote: The AGES-Reykjavik sample is drawn from an established population-based cohort, the Reykjavik Study.
note: A population-based cohort of older Icelanders drawn from the Reykjavik Study, phenotyped across cardiovascular, neurocognitive, musculoskeletal and metabolic systems to study disease and disability in old age. 'Gene/Environment' in the name refers to risk factors and gene-environment interaction in general, not to a defined exposure or an exposure-measurement design; the purpose spans many diseases, so not a disease cohort.

label: Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
diseases: dementia | Alzheimer's disease | Lewy body disorders
quote: The SADRC cohort is a longitudinal observational study of clinical dementia subjects and age-sex-matched non-demented subjects.
note: The Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center's observational cohort of people with Alzheimer disease, Lewy body disorders or mild cognitive impairment and matched non-demented controls, focused on Alzheimer disease and Lewy body disorders. A disease cohort with controls; no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: The cohort is of clinical dementia subjects with matched controls, and the centre's focus is 'Alzheimer's disease and the spectrum of Lewy body disorders', so the verdict and diseases stand; but the source's 'spectrum of Lewy body disorders' is broader than Lewy body dementia.

label: Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
quote: The CLSA recruited participants between 2010 and 2015 who were between the ages of 45–85 years to investigate social, environmental, and other factors that affect aging and disease.
note: A national stratified sample of 51,338 Canadians aged 45-85 assembled as a longitudinal platform for research on health and aging. A general population cohort with a broad purpose: 'environmental' factors are one of many measured, not a design purpose, and no single disease is studied.

label: Jackson Heart Study
quote: JHS is a prospective population-based observational study designed to investigate risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD) in Black individuals.
note: Community-based cohort of African American adults in Jackson, Mississippi, designed to investigate risk factors for cardiovascular disease: a population study of one disease family, with no exposure-based selection or purpose.

label: UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project
quote: The UKB Pharma Plasma Proteome (UKB-PPP) cohort comprises plasma samples from 54,219 individuals, including 46,595 randomly selected participants, 6,376 consortium-chosen individuals and 1,268 participants from a COVID-19 repeat imaging study.
note: A mostly random sub-sample of UK Biobank participants profiled for plasma proteomics to map pQTLs; a general population biobank subset with no exposure or disease selection.

label: Mass General Brigham Biobank
quote: It collects biological samples and health data from consenting individuals at Massachusetts General Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital, and local healthcare sites within the MGB network66.
note: Healthcare-system biobank of consenting patients across the Mass General Brigham network, not selected for any disease; its interest in environmental context is geospatial and socioeconomic rather than a designed exposure study.

label: Cardiovascular Health Study
quote: The Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS) is a population-based, longitudinal study of coronary heart disease and stroke in adults aged 65 years and older.
note: Population-based cohort of older adults sampled from Medicare lists in four US communities whose stated objective is the onset and course of coronary heart disease and stroke; no exposure-based design.

label: Framingham Heart Study
quote: Whereas the FHS was originally conceived and designed to study the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, it has evolved over the years with staggering expanded breadth and depth that have far greater implications in the study of the epidemiology of a wide spectrum of human diseases.
note: Community-based multi-generational cohort of Framingham residents conceived and designed to study the epidemiology of cardiovascular disease, the archetypal population study of one disease family; no exposure-based design.

label: Rhineland Study
quote: We used data from the Rhineland Study, an ongoing population-based cohort study in Bonn, Germany, to perform a GWAS on circulating complex lipid levels and composition measured using the Metabolon Complex Lipids Platform.
note: Population-based cohort of Bonn residents aged 30 and over, run by DZNE, whose stated aim is what keeps people healthy or makes them resistant to disease in general, with neurodegenerative and age-related diseases named as one interest: a broad health-and-ageing purpose, not one disease and not an exposure design.

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition-Potsdam
quote: EPIC was developed to examine the relationships between diet, nutritional status, lifestyle and environmental factors, as well as the incidence of cancer and other chronic diseases lilke type 2 diabetes.
note: The Potsdam centre of EPIC, a population-based diet-and-cancer cohort in which initially healthy adults are examined for exposure characteristics such as nutritional behaviour; cancer is the disease the cohort was set up for, though the stated purpose extends to other chronic diseases such as type 2 diabetes, hence medium confidence on the disease verdict.

label: Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos
quote: The HCHS/SOL will recruit 16,000 men and women who self-identify as Hispanic or Latino, 18 to 74 years of age, from a random sample of households in defined communities in the Bronx, Chicago, Miami, and San Diego.
note: Community-based cohort drawn by random household sampling of Hispanic/Latino adults in four US cities, studying heart, lung, blood, sleep, kidney, liver, diabetes, cognitive, dental and hearing conditions together with immigration and acculturation: a broad multi-disease purpose, not an exposure design.

label: Busselton Health Study
quote: The BHS is a community-based study in Western Australia that includes both related and unrelated individuals (predominantly of European ancestry) and has been described in more detail elsewhere46–48.
note: Community-based survey of residents of Busselton, Western Australia, run since 1966 and used for cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic and ageing research: a general population cohort with no single disease or exposure purpose.

label: Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-Based Life-Course and Environmental Research
quote: The Swedish Infrastructure for Medical Population-Based Life-Course and Environmental Research (SIMPLER; https://www.simpler4health.se/w/sh/en) includes data from two large, ongoing population-based studies: the Cohort of Swedish Men (COSM) and the Swedish Mammography Cohort (SMC)58.
note: Research infrastructure combining two population-based Swedish cohorts (COSM and SMC) whose stated purpose is research on dietary and lifestyle factors and genetics in relation to health in later life; the diet-and-lifestyle purpose makes it an exposure-designed aggregation, while its health outcomes are broad rather than one disease.

label: Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study
diseases: cardiovascular disease | chronic obstructive pulmonary disease | metabolic disorders
quote: The Swedish CArdioPulmonary BioImage Study (SCAPIS) was initiated as a major joint national effort in Sweden to reduce mortality and morbidity from cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and related metabolic disorders, all of which are important issues for public health.
note: Randomly recruited national population cohort of Swedes aged 50-64 whose stated purpose is cardiopulmonary disease (cardiovascular disease and COPD with related metabolic disorders); treated as a population study of a named disease family rather than a broad chronic-disease cohort, hence medium confidence. No exposure-based design. Checked 2026-09-25: A random population sample whose stated purpose is cardiovascular disease, COPD and related metabolic disorders; the quote is verbatim, but it names the related metabolic disorders as a third target, which the list left out.

label: Malmö Offspring Study
quote: The study participants of MOS consists of invited adult children and grandchildren to participants in the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study—Cardiovascular Cohort (MDCS-CC, n = 6103), which is a random, deeply phenotyped subpopulation of the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study (MDCS) [17].
note: Family-based cohort of the adult children and grandchildren of a random Malmö population sample, mapping risk factors for family traits of chronic diseases in general; diet is one of many measured factors, not the defining or main subject.

label: Metabolic Syndrome in Men Study
quote: METSIM is a study of 10,197 Finnish men from Kuopio in the late-settlement region of northeast Finland designed to investigate factors associated with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases3 (Supplementary Table 2).
note: Population-based cohort of Finnish men designed to investigate risk factors for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, the cardiometabolic disease family its name (Metabolic Syndrome in Men) points to; medium confidence because the purpose spans two related diseases. No exposure-based design.

label: Qatar Genome Program
quote: The QGP is a population-based study designed to perform whole genome sequencing of the Qatar Biobank (QBB) participants9 with the aim to gain insights into the population structure and the genetic architecture of clinically relevant phenotypes in the Middle Eastern Qatari population.
note: National whole-genome sequencing programme of Qatar Biobank volunteers to characterise the Qatari population; a population biobank with no disease or exposure selection.

label: Trøndelag Health Study
quote: In the HUNT Study, all residents aged ≥20 years in the Nord-Trøndelag region, Norway, have been invited to repeated surveys since 1984-86.
note: Total-population health survey of all adult residents of Trøndelag County, Norway, covering a broad range of health topics; a general population cohort with no disease or exposure selection.

label: Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge
quote: Any individual living in the United States with a professional diagnosis (by a physician, psychologist, or therapist) of ASD plus their parents and an unaffected sibling are eligible to participate in SPARK.
note: Nationwide US cohort of individuals with a professional diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder and their family members, built to accelerate autism research; a patient (family-based) disease cohort with no exposure basis.

label: Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort Study
quote: The Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) Study is an ongoing, multicenter, longitudinal study of nearly 5500 adults with CKD in the United States.
note: Multicentre prospective cohort of adults with chronic kidney disease enrolled at seven US clinical centres to study progression of kidney disease and cardiovascular disease; a patient cohort, not exposure-defined.

label: Systematic and Combined Analysis of Olink Proteins
quote: Each SCALLOP member works on human study collections from the general population, clinical trials or patients with certain diseases such as coronary artery disease, rheumatoid arthritis, bipolar disease, heart failure, dementias or metabolic syndrome.
note: Consortium pooling Olink proteomics and genotype data from general population cohorts, clinical trials and patient collections of many unrelated diseases to map pQTLs; it collects no single disease and no exposure-based cohorts.

label: China Medical University Hospital Biobank
quote: The study participants were part of the China Medical University Hospital (CMUH) Precision Medicine Project, a systemic effort initiated in 2018 to recruit subjects and collect biospecimens from all patients who come to CMUH for medical visits [69,70].
note: Hospital-based biobank recruiting all patients attending China Medical University Hospital, Taichung, for medical visits, used for GWAS and PheWAS across hundreds of traits; unselected for any disease or exposure.

label: Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project
quote: The Religious Orders Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project are both ongoing longitudinal clinical-pathologic cohort studies of aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD).
note: Pair of volunteer cohorts of older adults enrolled without dementia, with annual evaluation and brain donation, whose stated purpose is Alzheimer's disease; a cohort set up to study one disease, not exposure-based.

label: Mayo Clinic Biobank
quote: Participants were all Mayo Clinic patients, 18 years of age or older and US residents.
note: Clinic-based biobank of unselected adult Mayo Clinic patients established to supply controls for case-control studies and a prospective cohort for common outcomes; no disease or exposure selection.

label: HOLBAEK Study
quote: The study population consisted of children and adolescents from the HOLBAEK Study (previously known as The Danish Childhood Obesity Biobank),17 including an obesity clinic cohort with a BMI above the 90th percentile for sex and age (BMI standard deviation score [SDS] > 1.28) according to a Danish reference; and a population-based cohort, recruited from schools in 11 municipalities in Zealand, Denmark.
note: Danish childhood obesity biobank combining an obesity clinic cohort of children and adolescents in treatment with a population-based reference cohort; obesity counts as a disease, so a patient cohort with controls, not exposure-based.

label: FinnGen
quote: The FinnGen study (https://www.finngen.fi/en) is an ongoing research project that utilizes samples from a nationwide network of Finnish biobanks and digital healthcare data from national health registers.
note: Nationwide Finnish biobank-plus-register study of about 500,000 people studying thousands of disease endpoints; hospital-based recruitment enriches it for disease in general but it is selected for no single disease and no exposure.

label: NIHR BioResource Rare Diseases Study
quote: Patients with rare diseases and their close relatives were enrolled into 15 rare disease domains approved by the Sequencing and Informatics Committee of the NBR.
note: Whole-genome sequencing cohort of patients with rare diseases (or extreme quantitative traits), their affected relatives and controls, enrolled at NHS hospitals for diagnosis and gene discovery; a patient cohort across 15 rare disease domains, not exposure-based.

label: Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Ageing
quote: Participants with AD (211) had neuropsychological profiles which were consistent with AD, and were more impaired than participants with mild cognitive impairment (133) or healthy controls (768), who performed within expected norms for age on neuropsychological testing.
note: Longitudinal volunteer cohort of people over 60 with Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment and healthy controls recruited for prospective research into Alzheimer's disease; lifestyle factors are one class of candidate predictor alongside imaging and biomarkers, not the cohort's defining or main subject, so not an exposure cohort. Checked 2026-09-25: Volunteers with AD, MCI and healthy controls were recruited for prospective research into Alzheimer's disease, so the verdict, role and diseases stand and the quote is verbatim; but 'cognitive disorder' is much broader than mild cognitive impairment.

label: PopGen Biobank
quote: PopGen currently pursues recruitment, sampling and processing activities in close collaboration with a multitude of clinical partners, covering cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric and environmental diseases.
note: A population-based biobank in northern Germany that ascertains patients across cardiovascular, neuropsychiatric and other complex diseases together with population controls. A multi-disease genetic-epidemiology resource with no exposure design, so neither an exposure cohort nor a cohort of one disease.

label: Diabetic Nephropathy Cohort
quote: DN cohort recruited 2080 outpatient participants with T2D from the diabetes centre (Chinese N = 1309, Malay = 411, Asian Indian = 360) in a regional hospital between March 2004 and December 2015 with the primary aim to study the development and progression of DN and the secondary aim to study the major cardiovascular diseases (CVD) in T2D patients.
note: Outpatients with type 2 diabetes recruited at a Singapore diabetes centre and followed for diabetic nephropathy and cardiovascular events; a patient cohort, with no exposure-based selection. Checked 2026-09-25: The cohort recruited outpatients with type 2 diabetes to study the development and progression of diabetic nephropathy; the verdict and mappings stand, but the old quote only said participants came from the cohort, while the full text states its recruitment basis and aim.

label: Singapore Study of Macro-Angiopathy and Micro-Vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
quote: A total of 2258 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were recruited at baseline.
note: A prospective cohort of patients with type 2 diabetes recruited in northern Singapore to study vascular function and diabetes complications; a patient cohort, not exposure-defined.

label: Women's Health Initiative
quote: The Women's Health Initiative (WHI) is a large and complex clinical investigation of strategies for the prevention and control of some of the most common causes of morbidity and mortality among postmenopausal women, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and osteoporotic fractures.
note: Postmenopausal women enrolled into prevention trials (low-fat eating pattern, hormone therapy, calcium and vitamin D) or a parallel observational study, followed for cancer, cardiovascular disease and fractures. The dietary arm is an assigned intervention rather than an exposure-defined design, and the purpose spans several disease families, so neither verdict is yes.

label: Study of Health in Pomerania-TREND
quote: To identify determinants of the anti-TSST-1 antibody response, we examined 976 participants of the German population-based epidemiological Study of Health in Pomerania (SHIP-TREND-0).
note: A population-based sample of adults from Western Pomerania recruited as the second SHIP cohort for general health research; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study
quote: KoGES includes the community-based Ansan and Ansung study, the urban community-based health examinee study, and the rural community-based cardiovascular disease association study.
note: A consortium of Korean population-based cohorts and a national biobank set up to study the genetic and environmental aetiology of common complex diseases. Environmental exposure data are collected among many variables, but the design is a general-purpose population resource, not an exposure or single-disease study.

label: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
quote: The Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity (NEO) study is designed to investigate the pathways that lead to obesity-related diseases and conditions in a population-based prospective cohort study of individuals aged 45–65 years, with an oversampling of individuals with overweight or obesity.
note: A population-based cohort from the Leiden area in which people with a BMI of 27 or higher were eligible, oversampling overweight and obesity, designed to trace pathways to obesity-related diseases. Participants were selected for a disease-risk state (obesity counting as a disease), not for an environmental exposure.

label: Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention
quote: The Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention is a longitudinal observational cohort study enriched with persons with a parental history (PH) of probable Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia.
note: Middle-aged adults enriched for a parental history of Alzheimer's disease dementia, followed for preclinical Alzheimer's disease; a cohort selected for disease risk, with no exposure basis.

label: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
quote: The WADRC, previously described92, is a longitudinal cohort study of memory, aging, and AD in middle and older-aged adults who were recruited into one of six subgroups: (1) mild late-onset AD; (2) mild cognitive impairment (MCI); (3) age-matched healthy older controls (age > 65); (4) middle-aged adults with a positive parental history of AD; (5) middle-aged adults with a negative parental history of AD; and (6) middle-aged adults with indeterminate parental history of AD.
note: The Clinical Core longitudinal cohort of the Wisconsin ADRC, recruiting people with mild Alzheimer's disease or mild cognitive impairment alongside healthy controls and middle-aged adults with a parental history of Alzheimer's disease; a disease cohort of patients and at-risk relatives, not exposure-defined. Checked 2026-09-25: The cohort recruits people with mild AD and MCI with controls and at-risk middle-aged adults, so the verdict and diseases stand; the old quote only gave the Clinical Core's purpose, not who is recruited, and 'cognitive disorder' is broader than MCI.

label: Food Chain Plus
diseases: metabolic inflammation | type 2 diabetes mellitus | obesity
quote: The Food Chain Plus (FoCus) cohort was launched in 2011 for population-based research related to metabolic inflammation.
note: A Kiel-region cohort of which three quarters were drawn at random from residents' registers and one quarter were patients with metabolic inflammation from the university obesity outpatient centre, set up to study metabolic inflammation and the diseases it drives. Nutrition profiling is one of many data layers rather than an exposure-centred design, so the exposure verdict is no; the single-pathology purpose and patient component make it a disease cohort. Checked 2026-09-25: A partly random population sample plus 25% patients with metabolic inflammation from the Obesity Outpatient Centre, set up for research on metabolic inflammation and the metabolic diseases (type 2 diabetes, obesity) it is linked to; the old quote listed aims spanning many unrelated comorbidities, which reads as a broad purpose, so it is replaced by the purpose sentence.

label: Amish Complex Disease Research Program
quote: To date, over 7000 Amish adults have participated in one or more of our studies as part of the Amish Complex Disease Research Program72.
note: A University of Maryland research programme collecting studies of the Old Order Amish founder population of Lancaster County on the genetics of complex diseases (osteoporosis, cardiometabolic traits, longevity). Its members are population and family studies across many diseases with no exposure design, so both verdicts are no.

label: BioVU
quote: In 2007, VUMC launched a biobank, BioVU, and the BioVU Consent form is provided to patients in the outpatient clinic environments at VUMC.
note: A practice-based biobank of DNA from leftover clinical blood of Vanderbilt patients linked to de-identified health records; donors are unselected for any disease or exposure.

label: Southall and Brent Revisited
quote: Southall and Brent REvisited: cohort profile of SABRE, a UK population-based comparison of cardiovascular disease and diabetes in people of European, Indian Asian and African Caribbean origins.
note: A population-based tri-ethnic London cohort set up in 1988 to compare cardiovascular disease and diabetes between European, South Asian and African Caribbean people, described more loosely in a 2024 paper as a study of ethnic differences in chronic disease. Taken as a population study of one cardiometabolic disease family; no exposure basis.

label: Gut-and-Liver Axis in Alcoholic Liver Fibrosis
quote: 558 adults with alcohol-related liver disease aged 19–82 years, matched with healthy controls recruited from the Region of Southern Denmark5.
note: Consecutively recruited patients with a history of harmful drinking and early alcohol-related liver disease, with matched healthy controls, from Odense within the EU GALAXY consortium. Selection on harmful alcohol use makes it an exposure-defined cohort, and the participants are patients with alcohol-related liver disease.

label: Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study
quote: The sample comprised 2776 participants (54 % female) from the Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study who had CVD risk factor data measured in childhood in 1980 (aged 3-18 years) and markers of preclinical CVD measured in adulthood.
note: A population-based cohort of Finnish children and adolescents sampled in 1980 and followed into adulthood to relate childhood cardiovascular risk factors to preclinical cardiovascular disease, as its name states. A general population cohort devoted to one disease family; no exposure basis.

label: Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland
quote: We conducted the analysis in a well-characterized population-based study of 5,675 patients after CRC diagnosis in Scotland.
note: A population-based case-control study of colorectal cancer in Scotland whose cases are followed for survival; the participants of interest are colorectal cancer patients, with no exposure-based selection.

label: China Kadoorie Biobank
quote: The China Kadoorie Biobank (CKB) is a population-based prospective cohort of >512,000 adults recruited from 2004 to 2008 from 10 geographically diverse regions across China.
note: A population-based prospective biobank of half a million adults from ten regions of China studying many diseases and risk factors; no exposure or disease selection.

label: All of Us Research Program
quote: The All of Us Research Program plans to enroll a diverse group of at least 1 million persons in the United States in order to accelerate biomedical research and improve health.
note: A national precision-medicine cohort enrolling a million diverse US adults with questionnaires, health records and biospecimens; a general population resource with no exposure or disease selection.

label: BioMe Biobank
quote: A snLVEF genetic risk score (GRS) was applied and cases of snLVEF were identified in 486 754 individuals across two population-based cohorts (BioMe Biobank and UK Biobank).
note: An electronic health record-linked biobank enrolling patients of the Mount Sinai Health System non-selectively; a general biobank with no exposure or disease selection.

label: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
quote: The longitudinal CARDIA study was initiated in 1985 with the recruitment of young adult participants (aged 18-30 years) equally balanced by female and male sex and black and white race at 4 field centers located in Birmingham, AL, Chicago, IL, Minneapolis, MN, and Oakland, CA.
note: A prospective cohort of Black and White young adults recruited in 1985-1986 at four US centres and followed into midlife for the development of coronary and cardiovascular risk factors and disease, as its name states. A general population cohort devoted to one disease family; not exposure-defined.

label: Health for Life in Singapore
quote: Participants were recruited from the Singapore general population11,13,14.
note: A population-based multi-ethnic cohort of 10,004 Singapore residents for precision-medicine research on diverse diseases; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Cleveland Family Study
quote: Index probands with a laboratory confirmed diagnosis of OSA, and at least two first-degree relatives available to be studied were recruited along with family members.
note: A family study built around index probands with laboratory-confirmed obstructive sleep apnoea, their relatives and neighbourhood control families, designed to study the familial basis of sleep-disordered breathing. A disease cohort of patients and their at-risk relatives; no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: CFS recruited index probands with laboratory-confirmed OSA together with their relatives (and neighbourhood control families) to study the familial basis of SDB, so most participants are relatives selected for familial risk; sleep apnea syndrome is narrower than sleep-disordered breathing.

label: deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort
quote: This study is based on whole-genome sequence data from the whole blood of 15,220 Icelanders participating in various disease projects at deCODE genetics.
note: A population sample of Icelanders recruited through deCODE's many disease-specific projects and its general-population deCODE Health Study, used for genome-wide studies of diseases and traits at large. A multi-disease national resource with no exposure design, so both verdicts are no.

label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
quote: We validated SOPs used in the PainOmics retrospective study to find -omics biomarker to stratify patients with chronic low back pain recruited in the second middle of 2014.
note: A multicentre retrospective case-control study of patients with chronic low back pain and pain-free controls run by the EU PainOMICS project; a patient cohort with no exposure basis. Checked 2026-09-25: PainOMICS is a case-control study of chronic low back pain patients and pain-free controls, as the verbatim quote shows; the verdict stands, but HP Low back pain is broader than the chronic low back pain the source names.

label: The Pomak cohort
quote: We use whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to capture the entire allele frequency spectrum in 2,893 samples from two Greek population-based cohorts, MANOLIS and Pomak.
note: A population-based cohort of adult volunteers from the isolated Pomak villages of northern Greece recruited within the Hellenic Isolated Cohorts to study the genetics of complex traits; no exposure or disease selection.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
quote: Participants in the GERA cohort were recruited from the adult membership of the KPNC health plan, a large integrated health care system that provides comprehensive medical services to four million members.
note: GERA is a general cohort of adult Kaiser Permanente Northern California health-plan members within RPGEH, genotyped as a resource for GWAS of diverse traits and conditions; participants were selected neither for an exposure nor for a disease.

label: Correlated Expression and Disease Association Research
quote: We collected peripheral blood as well as intestinal biopsies (ileum, transverse colon, rectum) from 323 healthy Europeans visiting the Academic Hospital of the University of Liège as part of a national screening campaign for colon cancer.
note: CEDAR is a panel of about 320 healthy adults recruited at a colon-cancer screening campaign in Liège whose blood-cell and gut transcriptomes serve as an eQTL resource; it was built to interpret IBD risk loci, but its participants are healthy volunteers rather than patients, so it is not a disease cohort, and no exposure defines it.

label: Generation Scotland: Scottish Family Health Study
quote: Generation Scotland (GS) is a large family-based cohort study established as a longitudinal resource for research into the genetic, lifestyle and environmental determinants of physical and mental health.
note: Generation Scotland is a family-based general-population cohort recruited through general practices as a broad resource for physical and mental health research; environment is one of many determinants and no single disease is its purpose.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy
quote: In the first phase of GENOA (Phase I: 1996–2001), sibships with at least two adults with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60 were recruited, and all siblings in the sibship were invited to participate regardless of hypertension status.
note: GENOA recruited sibships ascertained on at least two siblings with clinically diagnosed essential hypertension before age 60, to find genes for blood pressure and hypertensive target-organ damage; recruitment is by disease (hypertensive sibships, normotensive siblings included), and no environmental exposure defines the cohort.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts
quote: We used data from two general population birth cohort studies, Northern Finland Birth Cohorts 1966 and 1986 (NFBC1966 and NFBC1986).
note: The Northern Finland Birth Cohorts programme collects two general-population birth cohorts (1966 and 1986) followed from the fetal period for health and well-being; neither an exposure nor a disease defines them.

label: Taiwan Biobank
quote: To advance epidemiological and biomedical research, Taiwan launched its own biobank, the Taiwan Biobank (TWB), in 2012, which prospectively collected a wide variety of lifestyle behaviors, environmental risk factors, and family history of common, complex diseases in the general Taiwanese population and measured genetic information in the biobank participants.
note: Taiwan Biobank is a prospective population biobank of volunteers from the general Taiwanese population; it records lifestyle and environmental exposures among many variables without exposure being its design purpose, and it targets no single disease.

label: GeneRISK study
quote: We use data from the prospective GeneRISK cohort46 whose principal aim is to assess the impact of communication of genetic risk information of CVD to study participants.
note: GeneRISK is a general-population cohort of Finnish adults (population register, occupational health customers, blood donors) set up to test how returning polygenic and clinical risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease changes health behaviour; participants were not selected for disease, but the cohort's stated purpose is one disease family, so it is a population study of cardiovascular disease; no exposure defines it.

label: Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span
quote: We designed a multidisciplinary, community-based, prospective longitudinal epidemiologic study among socioeconomically diverse African Americans and Whites.
note: HANDLS is an area-probability community sample of Baltimore adults stratified by age, sex, race and poverty status to study how race and socioeconomic status shape age-related health disparities; socioeconomic status alone is not an environmental exposure under these rules, and its health outcomes are broad.

label: Mount Sinai Crohn's and Colitis Registry
quote: Patients with UC (n=484) or CD (n=464) and HCs (ages 18+, n=365) were recruited as part of a cross-sectional study, the Mount Sinai Crohn’s and Colitis Registry (MSCCR), between December 2013 and September 2016 from the outpatient and endoscopy units of the Mount Sinai Hospital.
note: MSCCR is a registry of about 1,500 adults recruited at endoscopy at Mount Sinai Hospital, mostly patients with ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease plus non-IBD controls, for molecular studies of inflammatory bowel disease; a patient series with controls, not an exposure cohort.

label: Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety
quote: The Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety (NESDA, www.nesda.nl) is a longitudinal, multi-site, naturalistic, case-control cohort study set up to examine the etiology, course and consequences of depressive and anxiety disorders.
note: NESDA recruited adults with current or remitted depressive and/or anxiety disorders, at-risk persons and healthy controls from the general population, primary care and mental health care to follow the course of these disorders; a case-control disease cohort with no defining exposure.

label: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
quote: The Health, Aging, and Body Composition (Health ABC) study11 was a prospective longitudinal observational study designed to assess the association of body composition with physical function and disability in older adults.
note: Health ABC enrolled community-dwelling adults aged 70-79 from Medicare lists and Black residents of Pittsburgh and Memphis to study body composition, functional decline and disability in ageing; a population cohort of older adults with a broad purpose, selected neither for exposure nor for disease.

label: Michigan Genomics Initiative
quote: Here, we describe the Michigan Genomics Initiative (MGI), a single-health-system biobank currently consisting of >91,000 participants recruited primarily during surgical encounters at Michigan Medicine.
note: MGI is a health-system biobank of adult patients consented mainly at surgery, enriched for many diseases but for none in particular; a broad disease-genetics resource, not a cohort of patients with one disease, and no exposure defines it.

label: Immune and Metabolic Markers during Pregnancy and Child Development Study
diseases: autism spectrum disorder | other neurodevelopmental disorders
quote: Although this cohort was ascertained for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and other neurodevelopmental disorders (DD), we gained novel insight into how maternal and fetal genetics shape levels of immune mediators in pregnancy.
note: IMPaCT is a case-control study of KPNC mother-child pairs oversampling children later diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder or other developmental delay, with general-population controls, to study maternal immune and metabolic markers in pregnancy; the cases of a case-control study make it a disease cohort, and no environmental exposure defines it.

label: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium
quote: Special features of the CHARGE consortium are the large overall sample size, the population-based recruitment of cohort members, the standardized methods of data collection, and the prospective follow-up for clinical events.
note: CHARGE collects large prospective population-based cohorts (AGES, ARIC, CHS, FHS, Rotterdam and later others) for GWAS meta-analysis across many cardiovascular and ageing-related phenotypes; its members are population cohorts and its stated purpose is methodological and broad (heart and ageing research), so it is neither an exposure nor a single-disease aggregation.

label: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study
quote: This study was carried out in 1082 subjects belonging to the Helsinki Birth Cohort Study, which consists of men and women born between 1934 and 1944, in Helsinki, Finland, representing a general population of elderly people.
note: HBCS is a birth cohort of all singletons born in two Helsinki maternity hospitals in 1934-1944, followed to study how early life shapes adult health; a general-population birth cohort, and the persistent-organic-pollutant analysis in one paper is a use of the cohort, not its design.

label: Generation R Study
quote: The study is designed to identify early environmental and genetic causes and causal pathways leading to normal and abnormal growth, development and health from fetal life, childhood and young adulthood.
note: Generation R is a population-based birth cohort in Rotterdam designed to identify early environmental and genetic causes of growth, development and health, naming environmental, endocrine, lifestyle and nutritional determinants as its main exposures of interest, and it is listed in the Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue; its outcomes are broad, so it is not a disease cohort.

label: 500 Functional Genomics
quote: The 500FG cohort is a population-based cohort of healthy individuals of Western European ancestry consisting of 237 males and 296 females with age range of 18-75 years.
note: 500FG is about 500 healthy adult volunteers recruited at Radboudumc to characterise variation in cytokine and immune responses; the host and environmental factors it examines (age, sex, BMI, season, vitamin D) are not environmental exposures in the sense used here, and healthy volunteers are not a disease cohort.

label: MyCode Community Health Initiative
quote: In 2007, Geisinger launched MyCode, a system-wide biobanking program to link samples and EHR data for broad research use.
note: MyCode is a health-system biobank of Geisinger patients consented for broad research use with EHR linkage and genotype and exome data; patients of an integrated health system without selection for one disease or for an exposure.

label: 23andMe research cohort
quote: All participants were drawn from the customer base of 23andMe, Inc., a direct-to-consumer genetics company.
note: The 23andMe research cohort is the company's consenting customer base answering online questionnaires; unselected consumers with no defining exposure or disease.

label: LIFE-Adult-Study
quote: The LIFE-Adult-Study is a population-based cohort study, which has recently completed the baseline examination of 10,000 randomly selected participants from Leipzig, a major city with 550,000 inhabitants in the east of Germany.
note: LIFE-Adult is a random population sample of Leipzig adults deeply phenotyped for major civilization diseases (metabolic, vascular, cognitive, depression, sleep, retinal, allergies); a broad multi-disease purpose in an unselected population, with no defining exposure.
