note: Patients with severe or refractory asthma recruited at specialist severe asthma clinics; the cohort has no controls of its own.

label: SNP Health Association Asthma Resource Project
quote: subsets of clinical trials within the Childhood Asthma Research and Education (CARE) network including individuals with mild to moderate asthma [21], and the Asthma Clinical Research Network (ACRN) participating in the NHLBI SNP Health Association Resource (SHARe) Asthma Resource project (SHARP), which included individuals with a range of asthma severity (mild to severely persistent) [22].
note: Participants of NHLBI asthma treatment trials. Some CARE trials enrolled children at high risk of asthma rather than with asthma (EVE supplement: 'children with physician-diagnosed asthma or those at high risk for asthma'), but most participants have asthma.

label: Tomsk Study
quote: Both nuclear families and extended pedigrees were recruited through atopic bronchial asthmatic probands.
note: A family study ascertained through probands with atopic bronchial asthma, with their relatives; classified as patients, as COHO does for other asthma family collections (EGEA, SLSJ, BAGS). 'atopic bronchial asthma' is a new disease name for distinct_diseases_mapped.csv.

label: UFA Study
quote: The study involved 358 unrelated patients with physician-diagnosed bronchial asthma and 369 disease-free control subjects of different ethnicity (Russians, Tatars, and Bashkirs).
note: A case-control study whose cases are patients with physician-diagnosed asthma.

label: Genetics of Asthma International Network
quote: Probands aged 7-35 years with physician diagnosed asthma and symptomatic siblings were identified in 1022 nuclear families from 11 centres in six countries forming the Genetics of Asthma International Network.
note: A family study ascertained through probands with physician-diagnosed asthma and their symptomatic siblings; classified as patients, as COHO does for other asthma family collections.

label: Karelia Allergy Study
quote: The Karelia Allergy Study was initiated 23 years ago to study the prevalence of allergies and asthma in adjacent geographically similar regions—Russian (RUS) and Finnish (FIN) Karelia.
note: Randomly selected population samples on both sides of the border, studied for the prevalence and causes of allergy and asthma.

label: Kursk State Medical University Study
quote: KSMU: is a population‐based case‐control study of adult cases of asthma and controls matched for age and sex.
note: A case-control study whose cases are adult patients with asthma recruited at a pulmonology department.

label: Leukotriene Modifier Or Corticosteroid or Corticosteroid-Salmeterol Trial
quote: We randomly assigned 500 patients with asthma that was well controlled by inhaled fluticasone (100 microg twice daily) to receive continued fluticasone (100 microg twice daily) (169 patients), montelukast (5 or 10 mg each night) (166 patients), or fluticasone (100 microg) plus salmeterol (50 microg) each night (165 patients).
note: A treatment trial in patients with asthma.

label: Effectiveness of Low Dose Theophylline as an Add-on Treatment in Asthma trial
quote: We conducted a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial in 489 participants with poorly controlled asthma randomly assigned to placebo, theophylline (300 mg/d), or montelukast (10 mg/d).
note: A treatment trial in patients with poorly controlled asthma.

label: Multicenter Asthma Genetics in Childhood Study
quote: The followMAGICS study is the follow-up study of the observational Multicenter Asthma Genetics in Childhood Study (MAGICS), which includes physician-diagnosed asthmatic children and young adults (age: 7–25 years)15 recruited from secondary and tertiary centers in Germany and Austria.
note: Children with physician-diagnosed asthma recruited at secondary and tertiary centres; its controls in the case-control sets are ISAAC children, not MAGICS participants.

label: MRC Asthma and United Kingdom Control panel
quote: MRCA‐UK: is a collection of nuclear families (207 families total number of subjects 783) ascertained throughaprobandwith≥Step3asthmaaccordingtoBritishThoracicSocietyguidelines76 andfourhundred and thirty seven non‐asthmatic UK controls (UK‐C)77 .
note: A case-control panel whose cases are children with asthma from families ascertained through an asthmatic proband (all childhood onset in GABRIEL Table 1), with non-asthmatic UK controls.

label: Study of Asthma, Genes and the Environment
quote: It is a general population-based cohort, composed of children at high and low risk for asthma, living in urban and rural environments in Manitoba, Canada.
note: A population-based birth cohort set up to study the early-life origins of asthma (design paper title: 'A novel study design to investigate the early-life origins of asthma in children (SAGE study)').

label: The Epidemiology and Natural History of Asthma: Outcomes and Treatment Regimens
quote: The TENOR study is a 3-year, multicenter, observational study of patients with severe or difficult-to-treat asthma.
note: Every participant was enrolled by a physician as having severe or difficult-to-treat asthma, so the cohort is a patient series.

label: Tasmanian Longitudinal Health Study
quote: The Tasmanian Longitudinal Health Study (TAHS) is a population-based cohort (n=8583) study of respiratory disease.
note: A whole-population sample of Tasmanian schoolchildren born in 1961, set up and followed to study respiratory illness (asthma, bronchitis, lung function) from age 7 into the sixth decade.

label: Genetics of Asthma in Latino Americans
quote: Based on interviews and questionnaire data, children were included in the study if they were between the ages of 8-40 with physician diagnosed mild to moderate-severe asthma and had experienced two or more symptoms in the previous two years at time of recruitment (including wheezing, coughing and/or shortness of breath).
note: Probands were recruited for physician-diagnosed asthma and enrolled with both biological parents (case-parent trios), so the cohort is a patient series with relatives.

label: Mechanisms of Progression of Atopic Dermatitis to Asthma in Children
quote: Inclusion criteria were: 1) aged 1–2 years upon enrollment; 2) gestation of ≥36 weeks AND 3) a diagnosis of AD (based on the Hanifin and Rajka Criteria for Atopic Dermatitis(19)), OR the parent(s)/legal authorized representative (LAR) indicates a positive response to each of the 3 questions from the Children’s Eczema Questionnaire (CEQ) (20).
note: Every child is enrolled with atopic dermatitis; asthma, food allergy and allergic rhinitis are the outcomes followed (the atopic march), so they are not asserted as the cohort's disease.

label: Nottingham Sib Pair Asthma study
quote: Association analysis in families recruited on the basis of affected sib pairs for asthma reveal significant association for both coding region polymorphisms with atopy.
note: Families were ascertained through pairs of siblings with asthma (the study's reference, PMID:12189166, which PMID:20372189 cites for it); its index cases served as childhood asthma cases in PMID:20372189.

label: Jamaican Adolescent Asthma Study
quote: The Jamaican Adolescent Asthma Study (JAAS) is a cross-sectional study on the prevalence of asthma and allergies in 897 Jamaican adolescents [29].
note: A prevalence study of asthma and allergies in adolescents drawn from a national birth cohort (all births of September-October 1986), so a population study of that disease family rather than a patient series.

label: Mexico City Childhood Asthma Study
quote: Children with asthma (aged 5–17) and their biological parents were recruited between June 1998 and November 2003 from a pediatric allergy specialty clinic at a large public hospital in central Mexico City, Hospital Infantil de Mexico Frederico Gomez.
note: Case-parent trios ascertained through children with asthma at an allergy referral clinic: a patient series with parents.

label: Proyecto Genes Candidatos en Asma
quote: A total of 836 unrelated asthma cases and 574 non-asthmatic controls were recruited from the Social Security Clinic and outpatient health centers in Cartagena from 2002 to 2005.
note: An asthma case-control study with families ascertained through asthmatic probands, so its cases are patients.

label: Industrial Cohorts Research Group
quote: INDUSTRIAL (the Industrial Cohorts Research Group): The study base consists of several pooled surveys on occupational asthma from Denmark and The Netherlands.
note: The group pools occupational asthma surveys and contributed prevalent asthma cases with industry-, sex- and age-matched controls, so it collects patients.

label: Wessex family study
quote: Briefly, the Wessex population consisted of families with at least two biologic siblings with a current physician’s diagnosis of asthma.
note: Families ascertained through at least two siblings with physician-diagnosed asthma on regular medication: a patient collection with relatives.

label: German Affected-Sib-Pair Study
quote: The German sib-pair study consisted of two hundred and one families, consisting of at least two children with confirmed clinical asthma.
note: Families were ascertained through at least two children with clinical asthma: a patient collection with relatives.

label: Epidemiologisch Preventief Onderzoek Zoetermeer
quote: To study the prevalence and determinants of rheumatic and cardiovascular diseases a population survey was conducted between 1975 and 1978 in two districts of Zoetermeer, a suburban metropolitan area near The Hague in The Netherlands.
note: A population survey of all residents aged 5 and over of two districts of Zoetermeer whose investigators state its purpose as rheumatic and cardiovascular diseases (PMID:2712610; its first reports are titled a study of risk indicators for cardiovascular diseases, PMID:7360293). Later papers call its focus chronic diseases in general (PMID:9143207, PMID:27239529), so the curator may prefer 'no'.

label: Exeter 10,000 Study
quote: EXTEND/PRB is an unselected population cohort of 11,074 participants, 8295 without known diabetes, recruited from the community and primary care in the South West, UK.
note: An unselected adult population cohort recruited through general practices and the community, with a broad purpose (type 2 diabetes, ischaemic heart disease, vascular function and healthy ageing in the table of PMID:29459775). That table also calls the sample 'enriched for patients with diabetes', which the cohort's own papers do not say; the curator may want to weigh it.

label: Genomic Research Cohorts for CCMB Diabetes Study
quote: We studied 955 type 2 diabetes mellitus patients and 399 ethnically matched control subjects (Indo-Europeans) from Pune, Maharashtra, Western India.
note: An aggregation of the CCMB group's Indian type 2 diabetes case-control material: WellGen patients with T2D (KEM Hospital, Pune) with normoglycaemic controls from the Pune Maternal Nutrition Study, plus the IDPP3; the quote is from the CCMB group's own earlier case-control study of these samples.

label: Kangbuk Samsung Cohort Study
quote: The KSCS is a prospective cohort study to evaluate the natural history, prognosis and genetic and environmental determinants of a wide range of health traits and diseases among Korean adults.
note: Adults attending routine health screening, studied for a wide range of health traits and diseases: a broad-purpose general population cohort.

label: Malmö Preventive Project echo study
quote: These subjects were randomly selected from groups defined by glucometabolic status: normal fasting plasma glucose (FPG) (≤6.0 mmol/L); impaired FPG; new‐onset Type 2 diabetes mellitus; and prevalent diabetes mellitus.
note: The echo subsample was drawn by glucometabolic status with the groups with impaired fasting glucose, new-onset type 2 diabetes and prevalent diabetes oversampled (PMID:20211303), to study heart structure and function in relation to glucometabolic status, so its oversampled strata are patients with diabetes; the normoglycaemic stratum is included as in a case-control design.

label: Greek NAFLD study
quote: The sample consisted of 134 patients with NAFLD and 217 controls.
note: A case-control study of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease; cases have moderate or severe hepatic steatosis on ultrasound.

label: Tromso-6 Migraine
quote: 660 migraine cases and 2,407 controls were genotyped and in included in this study.
note: A migraine case-control sample drawn from a population survey: cases met modified ICHD criteria or reported migraine, the other genotyped participants are controls.

label: Yonsei Avellino Corneal Dystrophy Study
quote: Yonsei Avellino Corneal Dystrophy Study (ACD)
note: From the study's name only: no source describes whom it recruited, so the role (patients rather than relatives at risk) is an assumption.

label: Family Study of Cocaine Dependence
quote: Cocaine dependent subjects were recruited from publicly and privately funded inpatient and outpatient chemical dependency treatment centers in the St. Louis region.
note: Probands have DSM-IV cocaine dependence and were recruited from treatment centres, with matched community probands and a sibling of each; addiction counts as a disease.

label: GenomEUtwin
quote: In this issue of Twin Research, we describe different facets of a European Community funded effort, GenomEUtwin, which capitalises on eight of the world's largest and best characterised twin registers and a multi-national population cohort, MORGAM.
note: An aggregation of population-based twin registers and a population cohort, set up to find genetic and lifestyle contributors to common diseases in general; twin registries and broad purposes are not disease cohorts.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg F3
quote: The KORA study is a series of independent population-based epidemiological surveys of participants living in the city of Augsburg, Southern Germany, or the two adjacent counties.
note: A population-based follow-up examination within KORA, whose platform purpose is broad. Its baseline survey S3 was a MONICA survey of cardiovascular risk factors (classified yes on COHO:0001977), but no source read states a disease purpose for the 2004/05 follow-up itself; the curator may prefer to align it with S3.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg F4
quote: The Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg (KORA) F4 study (2006–2008) is a follow-up survey of the population-based KORA S4 study (1999–2001).
note: A population-based follow-up survey within KORA, whose purpose is broad; no disease selects its participants.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg S3
quote: This cross-sectional survey covering the city of Augsburg (Germany) and two adjacent counties was conducted in 1994/95 to estimate the prevalence and distribution of cardiovascular risk factors among individuals aged 25 to 74 years as part of the WHO MONICA study.
note: A random population survey conducted as the third Augsburg survey of the WHO MONICA project (Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease) with the stated purpose of cardiovascular risk factors, classified like MONICA (COHO:0000118) and the Czech post-MONICA survey (COHO:0001642).

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg S4
quote: The Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg (KORA) study consists of population-based surveys and follow-up periods in the area of Augsburg in southern Germany.
note: A population-based KORA survey of residents of Augsburg and two adjacent counties; unlike S3 it was not a MONICA survey, and no source read states a disease purpose for it.

label: Normative Aging Study
quote: Briefly, the VA Normative Aging Study is a closed cohort of 2,280 male volunteers from the greater Boston area (Massachusetts), 21–80 years of age at study entry, who enrolled after an initial health screening determined that they were free of known chronic medical conditions.
note: Healthy male volunteers screened free of chronic disease and followed to study normal ageing; ageing is not a disease.

label: National Emphysema Treatment Trial
quote: The National Emphysema Treatment Trial is a multicenter, randomized clinical trial of medical therapy vs medical therapy plus lung volume reduction surgery (LVRS) for the treatment of patients with severe bilateral emphysema.
note: A randomised trial whose participants all had severe bilateral emphysema; genetic studies use them as severe COPD cases (PMID:19300482: 'Subjects in NETT had severe COPD').

label: Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy Controls
quote: To qualify, each control subject was required to be grade 0 on the FECD grading scale, have no family history of a possibly inherited corneal disorder (eg, FECD, keratoconus, stromal dystrophy), and have normal corneas with no abnormalities on slit-lamp examination apart from certain conditions judged not to affect FECD10 .
note: The unaffected controls of a Fuchs dystrophy genetics study, screened free of the disease; like other control series in COHO they are neither patients nor selected for risk.

label: Framingham Eye Study
diseases: cataract | diabetic retinopathy | macular degeneration | glaucoma
quote: During the period 1973--1975, 2675 out of 3977 still-living members of the Framingham, Massachusetts, study population, who have been under investigation for coronary disease risk factors since 1948 and who were in 1973--1975 aged 52 to 85, were given an eye examination stressing cataract, diabetic retinopathy, macular degeneration and glaucoma.
note: An eye examination of the Framingham population cohort designed around four eye diseases, a population study of one disease family like the Blue Mountains and Beaver Dam eye studies.

label: Twins Eye Study in Tasmania
quote: Unravelling the mechanisms underpinning important blinding diseases could allow preventative or curative steps to be implemented. Twin siblings provide a unique opportunity in biology to discover genes associated with numerous eye diseases and ocular biometry.
note: Unselected twins examined to find genes for blinding eye diseases, chiefly glaucoma through its endophenotypes ('we decided to break glaucoma down into its component measures or endophenotypes', PMC3855231), classified like the Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (COHO:0001347); the Australian Twin Eye Study aggregation (COHO:0001499) was classified no, so the curator may want to align the two.

label: Gene MSA CH
quote: This study recruited patients of northern-European ancestry, preferentially with a relapsing onset of MS, although individuals with all clinical subtypes of the disease participated, including clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing remitting MS (RRMS), secondary progressive MS (SPMS), primary progressive MS (PPMS) and progressive relapsing MS (PRMS).
note: Site sample of the GeneMSA case-control study: patients with multiple sclerosis of any clinical subtype, with unrelated controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: Gene MSA NL
quote: This study recruited patients of northern-European ancestry, preferentially with a relapsing onset of MS, although individuals with all clinical subtypes of the disease participated, including clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing remitting MS (RRMS), secondary progressive MS (SPMS), primary progressive MS (PPMS) and progressive relapsing MS (PRMS).
note: Site sample of the GeneMSA case-control study: patients with multiple sclerosis of any clinical subtype, with unrelated controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: Gene MSA US
quote: This study recruited patients of northern-European ancestry, preferentially with a relapsing onset of MS, although individuals with all clinical subtypes of the disease participated, including clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), relapsing remitting MS (RRMS), secondary progressive MS (SPMS), primary progressive MS (PPMS) and progressive relapsing MS (PRMS).
note: Site sample of the GeneMSA case-control study: patients with multiple sclerosis of any clinical subtype, with unrelated controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: IMSGC UK
quote: The MS subjects were recruited from three clinical sites: 453 cases from the UK (IMSGC UK) and 342 cases from the US (IMSGC US); the remaining 860 MS patients were recruited at Partners MS Center in Boston, MA (BWH).
note: The UK multiple sclerosis cases of the IMSGC's genome-wide data, analysed with healthy controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: IMSGC US
quote: The MS subjects were recruited from three clinical sites: 453 cases from the UK (IMSGC UK) and 342 cases from the US (IMSGC US); the remaining 860 MS patients were recruited at Partners MS Center in Boston, MA (BWH).
note: The US multiple sclerosis cases of the IMSGC's genome-wide data, analysed with healthy controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: EPIPARK
quote: This cohort was set up in 2010 to investigate the specificity of non-motor symptoms for Parkinson's disease.
note: A population-based cohort of Lübeck inhabitants, grouped from healthy to suspected early parkinsonism, with Parkinson's disease patients, set up to study non-motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease.

label: Parkinsonism: Incidence, Cognition and Non-motor heterogeneity in Cambridgeshire
quote: The PICNICS study recruited newly diagnosed cases of PD and parkinsonism resident in Cambridgeshire between 1 April 2008 and 31 January 2010.
note: An incidence and inception cohort of people newly diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or parkinsonism in Cambridgeshire, followed for progression.

label: Profiling Parkinson's disease
quote: Patients were recruited from neurology clinics of university and regional hospitals in the western part of The Netherlands and all fulfilled the United Kingdom Parkinson’s disease Society Brain Bank criteria for idiopathic PD
note: A hospital-based cohort of patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease followed annually for five years.

label: Gothenburg Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: Additional DNA samples from CeAD patients of European origin were collected in 2010-2011 following CADISP inclusion criteria (Supplementary Fig. 1), through departments of neurology specialized in stroke care in Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Italy, France, Switzerland and the USA (Supplementary Table 4).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements of the Supplementary Note), who formed the Swedish part of the follow-up sample of CeAD cases collected under CADISP inclusion criteria; the SAHLSIS controls are not part of the collection.

label: Virginia Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: To increase the sample size for genetic analyses, an independent sample of 501 CeAD patients of European origin was recruited between 2008 and 2010, in some CADISP centers and additional 12 centers in 7 European countries and the United States (Supplementary Fig. 2), applying the same inclusion criteria as for the CADISP study (Supplementary Fig. 1).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements) at the University of Virginia, which contributed CeAD patients recruited under CADISP inclusion criteria to CADISP-2 (Charlottesville is a CADISP-2 centre) and to the follow-up sample.

label: Utah Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: To increase the sample size for genetic analyses, an independent sample of 501 CeAD patients of European origin was recruited between 2008 and 2010, in some CADISP centers and additional 12 centers in 7 European countries and the United States (Supplementary Fig. 2), applying the same inclusion criteria as for the CADISP study (Supplementary Fig. 1).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements) at University Hospital, Salt Lake City, whose patients, recruited under CADISP inclusion criteria, were part of CADISP-2.

label: Spanish Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: To increase the sample size for genetic analyses, an independent sample of 501 CeAD patients of European origin was recruited between 2008 and 2010, in some CADISP centers and additional 12 centers in 7 European countries and the United States (Supplementary Fig. 2), applying the same inclusion criteria as for the CADISP study (Supplementary Fig. 1).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements) in Barcelona, which contributed CeAD patients recruited under CADISP inclusion criteria to CADISP-2 (Barcelona is a CADISP-2 centre) and cases with controls to the follow-up sample.

label: Nijmegen Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: Additional DNA samples from CeAD patients of European origin were collected in 2010-2011 following CADISP inclusion criteria (Supplementary Fig. 1), through departments of neurology specialized in stroke care in Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Italy, France, Switzerland and the USA (Supplementary Table 4).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements) at Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre, who formed the Dutch Nijmegen part of the follow-up sample of CeAD cases collected under CADISP inclusion criteria.

label: Muenster Cervical Artery Dissection Collection
quote: To increase the sample size for genetic analyses, an independent sample of 501 CeAD patients of European origin was recruited between 2008 and 2010, in some CADISP centers and additional 12 centers in 7 European countries and the United States (Supplementary Fig. 2), applying the same inclusion criteria as for the CADISP study (Supplementary Fig. 1).
note: A collection of cervical artery dissection patients (so named in the acknowledgements) at the University of Münster, a CADISP-2 recruiting centre, whose patients were recruited under CADISP inclusion criteria.

label: Genetic influences on severity of COVID-19 illness in Korea
quote: Here we describe the results of three genome-wide association meta-analyses that consist of up to 49,562 patients with COVID-19 from 46 studies across 19 countries.
note: A Korean case-control study of COVID-19 severity contributed to the COVID-19 HGI; the quote describes the HGI's contributing studies collectively, and no printable text describes this study's own recruitment beyond its name ('severity of COVID-19 illness'), as for the other Korean HGI study, Corea (COHO:0001625).

label: Val Gardena COVID-19 study
quote: At the end of May 2020, we surveyed 2244 inhabitants of the Gardena valley representative of the local population, measured antibody test response to SARS-CoV-2 and related that response to symptoms, prior conditions and serum neutralisation capacity.
note: A random population sample of a valley hit hard early in the pandemic, surveyed for SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence and the determinants of infection and COVID-19 symptoms: a population study of one infectious disease, as for the Tirschenreuth Study (COHO:0000970).

label: Genomic epidemiology of SARS-Cov-2 and host genetics in Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19)
quote: We leverage a pandemic tracking strategy in which we sequence viral and host genomes and transcriptomes from nasopharyngeal swabs of 1049 individuals (736 SARS-CoV-2 positive and 313 SARS-CoV-2 negative) and integrate them with digital phenotypes from electronic health records from a diverse catchment area in Northern California.
note: Patients tested for SARS-CoV-2 at Stanford Health Care, the positives (cases) compared with the negatives for host, viral and clinical correlates of COVID-19 severity.

label: Determining the Molecular Pathways and Genetic Predisposition of the Acute Inflammatory Process Caused by SARS-CoV-2
quote: Whole blood samples from SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR negative (101) and positive lab tested individuals (473) were obtained from two clinical centers (Hospital Clínico Universitario de Valladolid, discovery cohort and Hospital Regional Universitario de Málaga, replication cohort).
note: Patients with RT-PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection sampled on arrival at hospital emergency wards, with PCR-negative individuals as controls, to study COVID-19 severity.

label: Mount Sinai Health System COVID-19 Genomics Initiative
quote: Here we describe the results of three genome-wide association meta-analyses that consist of up to 49,562 patients with COVID-19 from 46 studies across 19 countries.
note: A COVID-19 host genetics case-control study contributing cases with reported SARS-CoV-2 infection and controls to the HGI; the quote describes the HGI's contributing studies collectively (as for Corea, COHO:0001625), since no printable text describes this study's own recruitment.

label: Nanjing and Beijing Lung Cancer Studies
quote: The study subjects were from an ongoing two-center GWAS of lung cancer in China, including Nanjing study and Beijing study.
note: A lung cancer case-control GWAS: histopathologically or cytologically confirmed cases and frequency-matched controls.

label: Liverpool Lung Project
quote: Briefly, the LLP is a population-based case control and cohort study of the early detection of lung cancer in Liverpool, United Kingdom.
note: A population-based project set up to study lung cancer: a prospective cohort drawn at random from general practice registers in an area of high lung cancer incidence, plus a case-control study whose cases are lung cancer patients; 'patients' would fit the case-control arm alone.

label: Lung Cancer Study from Estonia
quote: the lung cancer study from Estonia, a hospital-based case-control study including lung cancer cases enrolled between 2002 and 2006 in Estonian hospitals and controls randomly selected from the Estonian Genome Project population-based cohort.
note: Hospital-based lung cancer case-control study: incident lung cancer cases from Estonian hospitals against Estonian Genome Project controls.

label: Lung Cancer in the Young study
quote: The LUCY-study provides access to a nationwide, population based family and a case-control sample (control population KORA, described below) of lung cancer patients aged 50 years or younger at diagnosis.
note: Patients with lung cancer diagnosed at 50 or younger, with their relatives; the relatives would be 'at risk', but the study is built on the patients.

label: Myaesthenia Gravis GWAS
quote: MG_GWAS (Myaesthenia Gravis GWAS) These genome-wide data were obtained from healthy Norwegian individuals recruited through the Norwegian Bone Marrow Donor Registry held at the Institute of Immunology, Oslo University Hospital, Norway (http://www.nordonor.org/).
note: Healthy controls from the bone marrow donor registry, genotyped by the Myasthenia Gravis Genetic Consortium and shared as external controls; despite its name the set holds no patients.

label: Réseau Français de la Génétique de la Sclérose En Plaques
quote: This sample was retrieved from REFGENSEP register of MS cases collected in 23 French hospital centers from 1992 to 2017.
note: A national register of people with multiple sclerosis, with their parents and siblings in trio and multiplex families.

label: Prognostic Genetic factors in Multiple Sclerosis
quote: A total of 1347 consecutive Italian MS patients diagnosed according to McDonald criteria [4], were ascertained by two Italian consortia, PROGEMUS (N = 1002), and PROGRESSO (N = 345).
note: Consecutive patients with multiple sclerosis recruited through hospital MS clinics; whether PROGEMUS itself recruited controls is unclear (the Italian controls of the IMSGC and later studies are pooled across consortia).

label: Norwegian Bone Marrow Donor Registry
quote: We report HLA-A, -C, -B, -DRB1, -DQB1 and -DPB1 allele frequencies and estimated haplotype frequencies from 4514 healthy Norwegians who volunteered to participate in the Norwegian Bone Marrow Donor Registry.
note: Healthy volunteer donors, used as population controls.

label: ADDITION-Ely Case-Control Study
quote: Previously undiagnosed prevalent cases of T2D, defined using World Health Organization oral glucose tolerance testing criteria, were identified via a population-based stepwise screening strategy among 40- to 69-y olds participating in the UK Cambridge arm of the ADDITION study.
note: A type 2 diabetes case-control study: its cases have screen-detected type 2 diabetes (T2D in the source) and its controls are Ely Study participants free of diabetes by oral glucose tolerance test.

label: Partners/Roche Cohort
quote: We obtained fasting blood samples and measured HbA1c, GA, and direct LDL-C, as well as other parameters, in a multi-ethnic population of 616 male and female patients with type 2 diabetes and 895 non-diabetic controls.
note: A sample of patients with type 2 diabetes and non-diabetic controls recruited by the Massachusetts General Hospital Diabetes Center and Brigham and Women's Hospital; its patients are type 2 diabetes cases in the MAGIC analyses.

label: Stanford Insulin Suppression Test Cohort
quote: The sample was drawn from multiple studies of insulin resistance at Stanford over the last ~10 years
note: Non-diabetic volunteers pooled from Stanford studies of insulin resistance, a physiological trait measured directly by the insulin suppression test; the cohort is not selected for a disease.

label: EPIC Obesity study
quote: The EPIC Obesity study comprises a representative sample (n = 2,566) nested within the EPIC-Norfolk Study27, a population-based cohort study of 25,663 men and women of European descent aged 39–79 y recruited in Norfolk, UK between 1993 and 1997.
note: A random, representative sample of a general population cohort, genotyped as the 'EPIC Obesity study' for genome-wide association studies of BMI and obesity; the name states obesity as its subject (as for other population samples genotyped for obesity, such as COHO:0001400).

label: Essen Obesity Study
quote: 487 extremely obese children and adolescents (‘cases’) were recruited in hospitals specialized for the inpatient treatment of extreme obesity (Table 2; mean BMI Z score: 4.63±2.27) while 442 healthy lean individuals (‘controls’) were ascertained at the University of Marburg (Table 2).
note: Extremely obese children and adolescents recruited through hospitals for inpatient obesity treatment, with lean controls, and obese offspring with their parents; obesity counts as a disease.

label: Fleurbaix-Laventie Ville Santé II study
quote: The Fleurbaix Laventie Ville Santé II Study includes 224 nuclear families recruited in 1999 and representative of the Northern France general population.
note: A community-based sample of families representative of the general population, whose stated aim is the determinants of adiposity and of weight and adiposity changes (traits), not a named disease; the curator could read the aim as obesity.

label: European Special Populations Research Network
quote: The European Special Populations Network (EUROSPAN) consortium consists of five population samples: (i) the Erasmus Ruchpen Family (ERF) study conducted in The Netherlands, (ii) the MICROS study conducted in Italy, (iii) the Northern Swedish Population (NSP), (iv) the Orkney Complex Disease Study (ORCADES; Scotland) and (v) the Vis study conducted in Croatia.
note: A consortium of population samples from isolated European populations; it collects no disease-selected studies.

label: Linz Peripheral Arterial Disease Study
quote: From April 2000 to April 2002 we consecutively enrolled all patients with symptomatic chronic atherosclerotic PAD admitted to a single tertiary care hospital in Austria (Konventhospital Barmherzige Brueder, Linz).
note: Consecutive hospital patients with symptomatic chronic atherosclerotic peripheral arterial disease, with matched hospital controls free of atherosclerotic disease.

label: GMetS
quote: GMetS European (France) Cases 507 (334/173) 55.9 (9.9) N/A N/A 28.5 (3.9) Metabochip Controls 2,553 (1,134/1,419)
note: A case-control sample in DIAGRAM's type 2 diabetes meta-analyses, whose cases are type 2 diabetes patients; no source describes how they were recruited.

label: GenePD Study
quote: The GenePD study is an ongoing study of familial PD which recruits families with at least two cases of PD meeting diagnostic criteria.
note: Recruits families with at least two members with Parkinson's disease (familial PD), with some unaffected relatives; the disease is named at the source's level (PD), the familial ascertainment being the design.

label: Genome Wide Association Study in Familial Parkinson Disease
quote: Unlike previous studies that focused primarily on sporadic PD, we have performed the first genomewide association study (GWAS) in familial PD.
note: A case-control GWAS sample whose cases are familial Parkinson disease patients (one per multiplex family from PROGENI and GenePD) and whose controls are NINDS repository samples.

label: Parkinson's Research: The Organized Genetics Initiative
quote: As part of an ongoing study designed to identify genes contributing to PD susceptibility (PROGENI Study), subjects with PD were recruited through the Parkinson Study Group (PSG), a network of 65 participating clinical centers located throughout North America.
note: Families ascertained through a pair of siblings with Parkinson disease, with the affected members examined; a patient series of familial PD (the paper's glossary expands PD as Parkinson disease).

label: Genomic Imaging Göttingen
quote: Exclusion criteria were past or present psychiatric disorders according to ICD-10, a positive family history of psychiatric disorders, substance abuse during the last month, cannabis abuse during the last 2 weeks, mental retardation, dementia, neurological or metabolic diseases, and pregnancy in women.
note: Healthy young volunteers recruited by advertisement, with psychiatric, neurological and metabolic disease excluded; an imaging-genetics sample, not a disease cohort.

label: Systematic Investigation of the Molecular Causes of Major Mood Disorders and Schizophrenia
quote: Here we generate new and so far unpublished genome-wide SNP data from 2,266 clinically well-characterized patients with BD (∼76% BD type I) and 5,028 ethnically matched controls, derived from the MooDS (Systematic Investigation of the Molecular Causes of Major Mood Disorders and Schizophrenia) consortium.
note: An aggregation of case-control samples collected for bipolar disorder (this quote) and schizophrenia (the German samples 'collected by separate groups within the MooDS Consortium', PMC6432650, described there under scz_boco_eur); the consortium's name speaks of major mood disorders and schizophrenia.

label: Pritzker Neuropsychiatric Disorders Research Consortium
quote: For the NIMH/Pritzker GWAS, 1,177 BP I cases (473 sibling pairs and 231 unrelated individuals) from the NIMH and Prechter Repositories and 772 controls from the NIMH Repository (Table 1) were genotyped on the Illumina HumanHap 550K chip; 512,844 autosomal SNPs passed QC (see Methods) and had minor allele frequency (MAF)≥1%.
note: A bipolar disorder case-control sample whose cases all have bipolar I disorder: 1,130 from the NIMH Human Genetics Initiative repository and 47 from the University of Michigan Prechter repository, with NIMH repository controls.

label: Rotterdam-Clinic study
quote: Rotterdam Clinic NA NA Yes NA NA OCT Wisconsin/modified Int.
note: The study's row in Supplementary Table 2 ('Recruitment and ascertainment per study') of the IAMDGC GWAS: advanced AMD cases recruited via ophthalmology clinic, no intermediate AMD cases or controls; a patient series.

label: UWA, LEI & Flinders
quote: AMD cases were drawn from patients presenting to ophthalmology clinics across Australia (in particular the Lions Eye Institute, Western Australia; the Launceston Eye Institute, Tasmania; and the Flinders Medical Centre, South Australia) as well as from the population-based Blue Mountains Eye Study (BMES)6,30.
note: A case-control collection of AMD patients from Australian ophthalmology clinics and controls (IAMDGC Supplementary Tables 1 and 2); the quote is from a 2016 analysis of the Australian IAMDGC samples whose acknowledgements name the UWA, LEI & Flinders group.

label: UCSD study
quote: The remaining 1121 white study participants, including 744 patients with advanced AMD and 377 healthy controls, were enrolled at the Moran Eye Center at the University of Utah and the Shiley Eye Center at the University of California, San Diego.
note: A clinic-based case-control collection of patients with advanced AMD and examined controls.

label: Depression Case Control Study
quote: All participants in the DeNT and DeCC studies experienced two or more episodes of major depression of at least moderate severity.
note: A case-control study whose cases have recurrent major depression (at least two episodes of at least moderate severity, SCAN diagnosis); the own paper's title names recurrent major depressive disorder.

label: RADIANT
quote: RADIANT is an umbrella term for three studies which sought to understand genetic risk for MDD and factors affecting response to treatment; this comprised of the Depression Network (DeNT) study (Farmer et al., 2004), the Depression Case-Control (DeCC) study (Cohen-Woods et al., 2009) and the Genome-Based Therapeutic Drugs for Depression (GENDEP) study (Uher et al., 2009).
note: An aggregation of depression samples: recurrent major depression cases of DeCC and DeNT and depressed patients of the GENDEP pharmacogenetic trial, with healthy controls.

label: DEMOKRITOS study
quote: DEMOKRITOS * DEMOKRITOS Greece Triple negative breast cancer cases enrolled from 1997-2010 in hospitals serving geographical areas of Greece, including Athens metropolitan area, Thessaloniki, Ioannina, Patras, and Crete (Chania), in collaboration with the Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group (HECOG).
note: A case-control study whose cases are Greek women with triple-negative breast cancer, with Athens population controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: The Stefanie Spielman Breast Bank and the Columbus Area Control Sample Bank
quote: OSU* The Stefanie Spielman Breast Bank and the Columbus Area Control Sample Bank U.S.A. Incident triple negative breast cancer cases enrolled at The Ohio State University James Comprehensive Cancer Center between 2003 and 2011.
note: A case-control study whose cases are incident triple-negative breast cancer cases of the Ohio State University James Comprehensive Cancer Center, with clinic controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: EPI-NPC-2005 study
quote: Briefly, NPC patients were recruited from Sun Yat‐sun University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, China, according to the following criteria: (a) pathologically confirmed NPC; (b) under 80 years of age; (c) residence in Guangdong Province for at least 5 years.
note: Hospital-based case-control study whose cases are nasopharyngeal carcinoma patients of Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: NPC Genes, Environment, and EBV study
quote: We conducted a population-based case-control study of nasopharyngeal carcinoma in Guangdong Province and Guangxi Autonomous Region.
note: Population-based case-control study whose cases are incident nasopharyngeal carcinoma cases; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: FinnTwin16
quote: FT16 was initiated in 1991 to identify the genetic and environmental precursors of alcoholism, but later the scope of the project expanded to studying the determinants of various health-related behaviors and diseases in different stages of life.
note: A population-based twin birth cohort begun to find the precursors of alcoholism, later broadened to health behaviours and diseases in general; classified like FinnTwin12 (COHO:0001327), whose stated aim is substance use and abuse.

label: Older Finnish Twin Cohort
quote: Earlier questionnaires were mailed in 1975 and 1981 to all twins born before 1958 and living in Finland, identified from the population register of Finland; the 1990 third-wave questionnaire was targeted to twins born in 1930–1957 who had responded to either earlier questionnaire.
note: A population-register twin cohort surveyed for health and behaviour in general ('genetic and environmental determinants of common, complex diseases', PMID:12537859), not recruited for or dedicated to one disease.

label: Finland SO replication
quote: The MS cases have at least one parent born within SO, and anonymous population controls were collected from the Central Hospital of Seinajoki in Southern Ostrobothnia.
note: Multiple sclerosis cases with a parent from the high-risk isolate, with population controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: Southern Ostrobothnia isolate GWAS
quote: We included in our GWAS 72 cases with either both parents from the high-risk isolate or one parent from the isolate and positive family history of MS and genotyped them with the Illumina HumanHap300 chip.
note: Multiple sclerosis cases from the high-risk isolate, with matched population controls; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: Fudan-Huashan Study
quote: The stage 1 samples for the GWA scan included 1,999 T2D case subjects and 1,976 nondiabetic control subjects drawn from the Nutrition and Health of Aging Population in China (NHAPC) study (312 case and 815 control subjects), the Gut Microbiota and Obesity Study (GMOS) (82 case and 163 control subjects), the Fudan-Huashan Study (807 case and 339 control subjects), and the Beijing Diabetes Survey (798 case and 659 control subjects).
note: Known only as a type 2 diabetes case-control sample of the 2013 GWAS; its cases make it a disease cohort. How it recruited is not described in the main text.

label: Gut Microbiota and Obesity Study
quote: Five hundred pairs of age- and sex-matched subjects (overweight/obesity) and control subjects (normal-weight) were planned to be recruited.
note: A case-control study whose cases are overweight or obese adults (BMI of 24 kg/m2 or more) and whose controls are of normal weight; the cases make it a disease cohort.

label: Genetic Association Information Network

label: GAIN Major Depressive Disorder Study
quote: Within these studies, 1862 participants with a diagnosis of MDD and 1857 controls at low liability for MDD have been selected for genome-wide genotyping by the US Foundation for the National Institutes of Health Genetic Association Information Network.
note: A case-control study whose cases have a lifetime diagnosis of major depressive disorder (MDD); controls were selected for low liability for MDD.

label: Gwangju Alzheimer's and Related Dementias
quote: The GARD cohort was established in 2013 as a large‐scale, community‐based prospective study to investigate early risk and protective factors across the AD spectrum.
note: A community-based prospective cohort of older adults set up to study Alzheimer's disease (its profile also calls it a population-based study of dementia, and its name covers related dementias).

label: Japanese Genetic Study Consortium for Alzheimer's Disease
quote: Blood samples were collected by the Japanese Genetic Study Consortium for AD (JGSCAD): the members are listed in our recent publications.10, 11 The LOAD patients were clinically validated, and satisfied the criteria of the National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Disorders and Stroke-Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association for a diagnosis of probable AD.
note: A case-control collection whose cases are clinically validated late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD) patients meeting NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for probable AD.

label: Gene-Environment-Development Initiative
quote: As part of the NIDA-funded Gene-Environment-Development Initiative (GEDI) our goal is to identify exactly which genes, which environments, and which developmental transitions together predict the development of drug use and misuse.
note: A consortium of general-population longitudinal samples brought together to find which genes, environments and developmental transitions predict drug use and misuse; addiction counts as a disease, as for COHO's CADD and MCTFR.

label: Irish Affected Sib Pair Study of Alcohol Dependence
quote: This article is the first report of the Irish Affected Sib Pair Study of Alcohol Dependence, whose goal is to detect the genomic location of susceptibility loci for alcohol dependence (AD).
note: Probands and affected siblings with DSM-IV alcohol dependence, recruited to map susceptibility loci for it.

label: Gene-Diet Attica Investigation on childhood obesity
quote: The Gene–Diet Attica Investigation on childhood obesity (GENDAI) [3] was established to specifically explore the contribution of genetics and environmental factors in the development of childhood obesity.
note: A school-based sample of schoolchildren (not selected for weight) set up to study the genetic and environmental causes of childhood obesity.

label: Greek Health Randomized Aging Study
quote: The "GHRAS" study is aimed at investigating the interactions among socioeconomic, lifestyle, dietary, psychological, and biochemical factors determining the health status of elderly Greeks.
note: A randomly recruited sample of urban elderly Greeks studied for the determinants of their health status in general, with no disease of interest.

label: GenNet Study
quote: GenNet recruited African-American (n=1101) and European-American participants (n=1497) at two field-centers between 1995 and 2003, based on a hypertensive proband.
note: Families ascertained through a proband with high or high-normal blood pressure (upper 20th-25th percentile, 'a hypertensive proband'), with siblings and parents enrolled regardless of blood pressure; classified as COHO classifies the other FBPP networks (HyperGEN, GENOA) and the FBPP itself.

label: Japanese Millennium Genome Project
quote: The Japanese Millennium Genome Project comprises seven independent study cohorts for studies of cardiovascular diseases and related risk factors.
note: A combination of general-population and workplace cohorts assembled for studies of cardiovascular diseases and their risk factors, used above all for the genetics of blood pressure and hypertension.

label: Genetics Network Rheumatology Amsterdam
quote: Cases were recruited from the outpatient rheumatology clinics of the VU university medical center, the Jan van Breemen institute, and the AMC/University of Amsterdam, all situated in the Amsterdam region in the Netherlands. All cases had RA consistent with 1987 ACR criteria, and only those patients that were CCP positive were used in this study.
note: GENRA collected patients with rheumatoid arthritis (1987 ACR criteria) from three Amsterdam rheumatology clinics, with blood-donor controls; the quote is from GENRA's paragraph of the Raychaudhuri 2009 Supplementary Note.

label: United Kingdom Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics
quote: DNA samples for 3,838 RA cases and 2,719 healthy unrelated controls were made available from the UK Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics (UKRAG) consortium, a collaboration of six UK rheumatology research groups.
note: A collection of rheumatoid arthritis cases (1987 ACR criteria) with healthy controls, assembled by the UK Rheumatoid Arthritis Genetics consortium for genetic studies of the disease.

label: Genetic Etiologies of Primary-Open angle Glaucoma Study
quote: The GLAUGEN study contains POAG cases and controls derived from the Genetic Etiologies of Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (GEP) study, the Nurses’ Health Study (NHS), and the Health Professionals Follow-up Study (HPFS). The GEP is a clinical case-control study from Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary while the NHS and HPFS contain cases and controls nested within population-based cohorts at risk for POAG.
note: GEP is a clinic-based case-control study of primary open-angle glaucoma whose cases came from the Glaucoma Service of the Massachusetts Eye and Ear Infirmary.

label: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Genes and Environment Study
quote: The GLAUGEN study contains POAG cases and controls derived from the Genetic Etiologies of Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (GEP) study, the Nurses’ Health Study (NHS), and the Health Professionals Follow-up Study (HPFS).
note: A pooled case-control set of primary open-angle glaucoma drawn from the GEP clinic-based study and from cases and matched controls nested in the Nurses' Health Study and the Health Professionals Follow-up Study.

label: Genetic and Immunological Studies of European and African HIV-1+ Long Term Non-Progressors
quote: Here we performed a GWAS on a cohort of 160 HIV-1 infected Caucasian Long Term Non Progressors (LTNP) from the EC-funded European-African ''GISHEAL'' Consortium in order to explore whether novel genetic factors could account for the LTNP phenotype (i.e. maintenance of CD4 T cell counts >500 cells/μl and good health conditions without therapy).
note: A cohort of untreated HIV-1-infected long-term non-progressors; the participants have the infection, so it is a patient cohort, not an exposed-uninfected one.

label: Modena HIV Surveillance Cohort
quote: Under the auspices of the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV, we have combined the genome-wide single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) data collected by 25 cohorts, studies, or institutions on HIV-1 infected individuals and compared them to carefully matched population-level data sets
note: The Modena Cohort is one of the 25 cohorts, studies or centres of the International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV, which pooled genome-wide data on HIV-1-infected individuals; the quote states the design, and the list at the end of the same paper names the Modena Cohort. Its description in Text S1 ('HIV surveillance cohort' of new cases of HIV-infected adults) could not be re-read here.

label: Health2 T2D Study
quote: A total of 1,183 T2D cases were selected from population-based 'Health2 cohort'.
note: A type 2 diabetes case-control sample: cases with T2D (onset at 40 or older) from the Health2 cohort and normoglycaemic controls from Health2 and HEXA.

label: Health2 Study
quote: The Health2 study consists of community-based cohorts from 5 rural areas (i.e., Wonju, Pyeongchang, Gangneung, Geumsan, and Naju), and the HEXA study is a cohort from 14 urban areas.
note: A community-based population cohort of five rural areas used for many traits (type 2 diabetes, blood pressure, lipids, blood cells); its own sources state no disease purpose. Its parent CAVAS (COHO:0000629) is classified as a population study of cardiovascular disease from its name and purpose; if Health2 is merged into CAVAS this row goes.

label: Health Habits and Opinions study
quote: This Health Habits and Opinions study (HHO) assessed many of the same political attitudes in the HLQ.
note: A follow-up survey of adult twins from a population kinship sample, measuring health habits and political and social attitudes; no disease basis.

label: Mid-Atlantic Twin Registry
quote: The Mid-Atlantic Twin Registry (MATR) is a population-based registry of twin pairs ascertained from birth records and school system records of Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.
note: A population-based twin registry ascertained from birth and school records; twin registries are not disease cohorts even though studies recruited from them address many diseases.

label: Harvard i2b2
quote: Phase Sample Subjects MDD case Control Discovery GAIN 3461 1696 1765 GenRED 2283 1030 1253 GSK 1751 887 864 MDD2000-QIMR_610 1184 433 751 MDD2000-QIMR_317 1977 1017 960 MPIP 913 376 537 RADIANT + Bonn/Mannheim 2225 935 1290 RADIANT 3213 1625 1588 STAR*D 1752 1241 511 MDD replication deCODE 34 229 1067 33 162 GenPod/NEWMEDS 5939 477 5462 Harvard i2b2 902 460 442

quote: Cases and controls used in discovery and replication phases Phase Sample Subjects MDD case Control Discovery GAIN 3461 1696 1765 GenRED 2283 1030 1253 GSK 1751 887 864 MDD2000-QIMR_610 1184 433 751 MDD2000-QIMR_317 1977 1017 960 MPIP 913 376 537
note: A case-control sample of major depressive disorder: MDD inpatients of the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry hospital with community controls; the PGC table lists its MDD cases and controls.

quote: The framework is an adaptive phase II clinical trial design in the neoadjuvant setting for women with locally advanced breast cancer.
note: A neoadjuvant treatment trial whose participants are women with locally advanced, high-risk breast cancer.

label: Pathways Study
quote: Eligibility includes any woman diagnosed with invasive breast cancer within KPNC, no previous diagnosis of other invasive cancer, age 21 years or older, and ability to speak English, Spanish, Cantonese, or Mandarin.
note: A cohort of women newly diagnosed with invasive breast cancer, followed for recurrence and survival.

label: Kansas-City Osteoporosis Study
quote: The KCOS is a cross-sectional study of osteoporosis with 2,286 unrelated European ancestry participants living in and around Kansas City, Missouri, USA.
note: A study of osteoporosis in randomly recruited, otherwise healthy adults of the general population of the Kansas City area.

label: Omaha Osteoporosis Study
quote: This study used 11,315 randomly recruited Caucasian subjects, from three cross-sectional study cohorts: 5,939 from the Louisiana Osteoporosis Study (LOS, New Orleans and Baton Rouge area, Coordinates: ~30oN~90–91oW)39, 3,497 from the Kansas City Osteoporosis Study (KCOS, Kansas City area, Coordinates: ~39oN~94oW)40, and 1,879 from the Omaha Osteoporosis Study (OOS, Omaha area, Coordinates: ~41oN~96oW)41.
note: A cross-sectional osteoporosis study of randomly recruited, otherwise healthy adults of the Omaha area; the disease of interest is the one its name gives.

label: Liver Biopsy Cohort
quote: the Liver Biopsy Cohort (LBC; n = 1,951) consisting of individuals at risk for non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) from northern and southern Europe
note: Participants had liver biopsy for suspected NASH or for severe obesity; the cohort's papers describe them as individuals at risk of (progressive) NAFLD.

label: Swedish Obese Subjects Study
quote: The SOS is a prospective study comparing the effects of bariatric surgery and usual care in severely obese individuals in Sweden 22.
note: Participants are severely obese adults (BMI of at least 34 for men and 38 for women) treated by bariatric surgery or usual obesity care.

label: Pharmacogenomics of Metformin
quote: Included participants had a clinical diagnosis of type 2 diabetes and were treated with sulfonylureas as monotherapy or as an add-on to metformin.
note: Adults with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin or sulfonylureas, identified from Kaiser Permanente electronic records; the quote describes the participants of every cohort of the sulfonylurea meta-analysis, PMET among them.

label: Minority GWAS African American study
quote: The African American CRC cases and controls in this analysis are from seven studies/centers in the USA (Supplementary Material, Methods and Table S1).
note: An aggregation of African American colorectal cancer (CRC) cases and controls pooled from seven US studies for a genome-wide association study of colorectal cancer, classified by what it collects: CRC patients with controls.

label: Minority GWAS Japanese study
quote: The colorectal cancer GWAS among Japanese and African Americans was funded through US National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants 1R01-CA126895, 1R01-CA126895-S1, 1R01-CA104132, 2U24-CA074806.
note: A pooled genome-wide association study of colorectal cancer in people of Japanese ancestry, made of colorectal cancer cases and controls from six studies; classified by what it collects: colorectal cancer patients with controls.

label: Oxford Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Study
quote: The Oxford Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Study (OxAAA) prospectively recruited AAA patients undergoing the routine NHS management pathway.
note: A prospective cohort of patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm under surveillance or referred for surgery at the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford (a 2026 paper, PMID:41736891, also mentions healthy volunteers enrolled in the study for comparison).

label: Uppsala Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Cohort Study
quote: A prospective population-based case-control study which aims to find biomarkers for the cause and progression of AAA and investigate how persons with or without an AAA experience their health.
note: A population-based case-control study of abdominal aortic aneurysm built on ultrasound screening of 65-year-old men; its cases have AAA (only they were genotyped for the GWAS). It could also be read as a population study of AAA, since all 65-year-old men were invited.

label: Prevalence of osteoporosis in Slovenia
quote: 34 SLO‐PREVAL Prevalence of osteoporosis in Slovenia Cross‐sectional Population‐based Slovenia Ljubljana Central European 716
note: A cross-sectional, population-based study named 'Prevalence of osteoporosis in Slovenia', of premenopausal women aged 35-50 and postmenopausal women and men over 50, set up for genotype-phenotype studies of bone; its stated subject is one disease, osteoporosis.

label: Women's Health Initiative Genetic Components of HIP Fracture Consortium
quote: All hip fractures in the WHI Clinical Trial (CT) and Observational Study (OS) through Aug2007 were selected and matched to controls.
note: A genetic study of hip fracture nested in the WHI: its main portion is a case-control sample of all hip fracture cases of the WHI trials and observational study with matched controls; its BMD portion selected women on extreme hip BMD Z-scores and physical functioning (traits).

label: Transcontinental COPD Genetics Study
quote: We enrolled severe COPD subjects and smoker controls in Korea and Poland in the Transcontinental COPD Genetics Study (TCGS) and severe COPD cases in a study of frequent and infrequent exacerbators from the USA.
note: Case-control studies of severe to very severe COPD (FEV1 below 50% predicted) with smoker controls with normal spirometry, in Poland and Korea.

label: UK Biobank Lung Exome Variant Evaluation
quote: We sampled individuals of European ancestry from UK Biobank, from the middle and extremes of the forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) distribution among heavy smokers (mean 35 pack-years) and never smokers.
note: Participants were selected on a trait, lung function (the middle and extremes of FEV1), within heavy smokers and never smokers, for genetic studies of lung function, smoking behaviour and COPD; COPD cases were defined within the sample for secondary analyses, but nobody was recruited for having COPD, and traits are out of scope (as for the SpiroMeta consortium, COHO:0000695).

label: London and the South East Region Alzheimer's Disease Study
quote: An overview of the LASER-AD study: a longitudinal epidemiological study of people with Alzheimer's disease.
note: Every participant has Alzheimer's disease: a prospective cohort of people with the disease (and their carers) recruited through services in London and the South East.

label: MRC Prion Unit/UCL Department of Neurodegenerative Disease collection

label: Utrecht Health Project
quote: All new inhabitants are invited by their general practitioner to participate in the Utrecht Health Project (UHP).
note: A general population health-monitoring cohort of all new residents of a district, with a broad purpose (determinants of health and disease, use of healthcare); no disease of interest.

label: Wheezing Illnesses Study Leidsche Rijn
quote: The aims of WHISTLER are to investigate determinants for wheezing illnesses (including neonatal lung function, viral infections, asthma-susceptibility genes and endotoxin exposure) and to derive a comprehensive risk score, that is appropriate for use in primary health care and allows for efficient planning of early preventive strategies.
note: A population-based birth cohort of healthy newborns whose stated purpose is one disease family, childhood wheezing illnesses (the respiratory illnesses that include asthma).

label: Women's Circle of Health Study
quote: Study participants were breast cancer cases based on the Women’s Circle of Health Study (WCHS), a multi-site case-control study in New York City and New Jersey designed to investigate genetic and lifestyle risk factors for aggressive breast cancer.
note: A breast cancer case-control study: the cases are women with newly diagnosed breast cancer (controls are included, as in any case-control study).

label: Wisconsin Women's Health Study
quote: This analysis used data from the breast cancer cases enrolled in the Wisconsin women’s health study (WWHS), a federally funded population-based case–control study designed to examine the associations of lifestyle factors and genetics with breast cancer risk.
note: Population-based case-control studies of breast cancer: the cases are women with incident breast cancer from the statewide registry (controls are included, as in any case-control study).

label: Women's Health Initiative Hormone Therapy Trials
quote: Briefly, 27,347 postmenopausal women 50–79 years of age in areas surrounding 40 clinical centers were enrolled in one of two randomized, double-blind trials between 1993 and 1998.
note: Prevention trials in postmenopausal women selected by menopausal and hysterectomy status, not by a disease; menopause is not a disease, and the trials' outcomes span several diseases (coronary heart disease, breast cancer, stroke, fractures).

label: Women's Health Initiative Long Life Study
quote: The WHI-LLS was a single in-person visit conducted in 2012–2013 to collect phlebotomy, anthropometry, and objective physical function measures in WHI Extension Study Participants.
note: An ageing study of older women from the WHI Extension Study (blood, clinical and physical-function measures), not selected for or focused on one disease.

label: Estudio Familiar de Influencia Genetica en Alzheimer
quote: A cohort of Caribbean Hispanics with familial LOAD was recruited in a different study at the Taub Institute for Research on Alzheimer’s Disease and the Aging Brain in New York and from clinics in the Dominican Republic as part of the EFIGA study.
note: A family study built on patients with familial late-onset Alzheimer disease (LOAD) and their relatives, classified like the parallel NIA-LOAD family study (COHO:0000669); the unaffected relatives followed up are at risk, but the recruitment basis is the affected patients.

label: Emory Genebank Study
quote: The Emory Genebank Study was designed to investigate the relationship between biochemical and genetic factors with CAD in subjects undergoing cardiac catheterization.
note: Patients undergoing cardiac catheterization, studied for coronary artery disease (CAD), with angiographic CAD cases and catheterized controls without CAD; classified like the comparable catheterization biobanks in COHO (CATHGEN, Cleveland Clinic GeneBank).

label: European Male Ageing Study
quote: Subjects were recruited from population registers and those who agreed to take part completed a detailed questionnaire including aspects of personal and medical history, lifestyle factors and sexual function.
note: A population-register sample of men aged 40-79, set up to study the symptoms of ageing in men and their hormonal, genetic and psychosocial predictors; ageing is not a disease, and no disease defines recruitment.

label: Epidemiology of Functional Disorders
quote: We conducted a 4-year prospective population-based study of pain in the North-West of England known as the Epidemiology of Functional Disorders (Epifund) study.
note: A general-practice population sample surveyed by post to study pain (the papers analyse musculoskeletal pain, chronic widespread pain in particular); the source names the condition only as pain, so that is the entry. Compare the Danish Study of Functional Disorders (COHO:0001645), classified as a population study of functional somatic syndromes.

label: Johns Hopkins Epidemiology-Genetics Program Ashkenazi Jewish schizophrenia case-control sample
quote: Subjects included research participants with a diagnosis of SZ (including schizoaffective) or BP diagnosis recruited over a 15-year period (1996–2011) through advertisements, talks, letters to leaders service providers of the Jewish community and a study web site.
note: The cases of this case-control sample have schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder (124 of the 721 probands of the example paper are schizoaffective, PMID:20431428); the program's bipolar cases named in the quote belong to its other collections, not to this term.

label: EpiHealth
quote: Potential participants in the age group 45–75 years will receive information about EpiHealth and an invitation to participate in the study by postal mail.
note: Invited from the Swedish population aged 45-75, with no exclusions for disease; its outcomes are common degenerative disorders in general (cardiovascular disease, cancer, dementia, joint pain, lung disease, depression, fractures), a broad purpose.

label: EURODIAB Family Study
diseases: type 1 diabetes | diabetic nephropathy | diabetic retinopathy
quote: The objective of the EURODIAB FS is to identify genes and pathways involved in the pathogenesis of nephropathy (DN) and retinopathy (DR) in type 1 DM.
note: All participants have type 1 diabetes; the cases have diabetic nephropathy or proliferative retinopathy and the controls long-standing diabetes without them.

label: French-Canadian Family Study on Factor V Leiden Thrombophilia
quote: The family study is composed of five extended French-Canadian pedigrees, totaling 255 relatives, ascertained at the Thrombosis Clinic of the Ottawa Hospital through single probands with idiopathic VT and heterozygote for the Factor V Leiden mutation.
note: Relatives of probands with idiopathic venous thrombosis who carry the factor V Leiden mutation, so a family sample at risk of venous thrombosis (5.1% of the 214 with methylation data had had VT, PMID:25265411); the other papers call the probands' disease venous thromboembolism.

label: Fels Longitudinal Study
quote: Participants were not selected with regard to any known factors associated with health concerns, diseases or body composition.
note: A growth and development cohort enrolling children, usually at birth, and their families, without selection for any disease; its later papers study adiposity and liver fat, but no disease defines it.

label: FINRISK 1997
quote: FINRISK surveys have been conducted every 5 years since 1972 to monitor the risk of chronic diseases.
note: A stratified random population sample; the FINRISK surveys monitor chronic-disease risk broadly, as for the FINRISK aggregation (COHO:0000071, classified no). Consortium supplements describe FINRISK97 as 'designed to study the prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors in Finland' (ICBP 2011), which the curator may read as a population study of cardiovascular disease instead.

label: Flemish Study on Environment, Genes and Health Outcomes
quote: The Flemish Study on Environment, Genes, and Health Outcomes (FLEMENGHO) is an observational, community-based cohort study on cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes in the adult Belgian population.
note: A randomly recruited family-based population sample whose stated subject is cardiovascular risk factors and outcomes (the source's words; the HOMAGE paper, PMID:25332706, calls it 'a large-scale family-based study on the genetic epidemiology of cardiovascular phenotypes'), so a population study of cardiovascular disease, as for Framingham.

label: Framingham Offspring Study
quote: This study, called the Framingham Offspring Study (FOS), was undertaken to expand upon knowledge of cardiovascular disease, particularly in the area of familial clustering of the disease and its risk factors.
note: The children of the Framingham cohort and their spouses, examined to study cardiovascular disease and its familial clustering; like its parent, the Framingham Heart Study (COHO:0000385), a population study of cardiovascular disease. The offspring were not selected for their parents' disease, so not 'at risk'.

label: German Alzheimer's disease Integrated Genome Research Network
quote: Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) which remained significant at P≤1×10−5 were then tested for replication in the second stage of this study, comprising 4896 cases and 4903 controls including genotyping of the GERAD2 sample and in silico replication in the deCODE and German Alzheimer’s disease Integrated Genome Research Network (AD-IG) GWAS datasets.
note: AD-IG is a German genome-wide association dataset of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls, used as an in silico replication dataset in GERAD+; the quote names it as an Alzheimer's disease GWAS dataset contributing cases and controls to the study's second stage.

label: Bipolar Disorder Genetic Association Information Network
quote: To identify bipolar disorder (BD) genetic susceptibility factors, we conducted two genome-wide association (GWA) studies: one involving a sample of individuals of European ancestry (EA; n=1001 cases; n=1033 controls), and one involving a sample of individuals of African ancestry (AA; n=345 cases; n=670 controls).
note: GAIN-BP is the case-control sample of a genome-wide association study of bipolar disorder: unrelated cases with bipolar disorder from the NIMH Genetics Initiative collections with matched controls.

label: Genetic Architecture of Smoking and Smoking Cessation
quote: The overall goal of this project is to identify and characterize genetic variants that contribute to the development of nicotine dependence, related smoking behaviors, and smoking cessation.
note: A case-control dataset whose cases are nicotine-dependent smokers (FTND score of 4 or more) and whose controls are smokers who never became dependent; nicotine dependence is an addiction and counts as a disease.

label: Australian Genetics of Bipolar Disorder Study
quote: To address these questions, we established a nation-wide cohort of 6682 adults living with BD in Australia.
note: Every participant was recruited as an adult living with bipolar disorder (media campaign, a mail-out to people dispensed lithium carbonate, and depression-study participants reporting bipolar disorder), and the study's purpose is genetic risk, treatment response and adverse drug reactions in bipolar disorder.

label: CBDB/NIMH Genetic Study of Schizophrenia
quote: We studied 169 patients with schizophrenia, 213 of their unaffected siblings, and 212 healthy volunteers from the CBDB/NIMH Genetic Study of Schizophrenia with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
note: An ongoing NIMH family study of schizophrenia that recruits patients with schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder together with their unaffected siblings and healthy volunteers, to find intermediate phenotypes and risk genes for the illness; the patients make it a patients cohort (its siblings would also qualify as at risk).

label: Genetic Lung Cancer Predisposition Study
quote: All patients diagnosed with lung cancer between March 1999 and July 2004 were eligible for the study.
note: A case-control DNA resource whose cases are patients diagnosed with lung cancer and whose controls are their spouses or partners without a history of cancer, established to find low-penetrance susceptibility alleles for lung cancer.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine Study
quote: The Leiden sample is a well-phenotyped population-based migraine cohort from the Genetic Epidemiology of Migraine (GEM) study from the Netherlands.
note: A population-based sample drawn at random from two Dutch county registries whose whole purpose is migraine: every participant was screened on headache history, screen-positives given a headache questionnaire and a random subset a clinical interview, with migraine diagnosed by International Headache Society criteria.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Metabolic Syndrome Study
quote: Eligible families consisted of a minimum of two siblings (an affected sib-pair) with atherogenic dyslipidemia (ADL), which was defined by the simultaneous presence of high triglyceride (≥75% percentile for age, sex, and country) and low HDL-cholesterol (HDL-C) (≤25% percentile for age, sex, and country) levels in plasma.
note: Ascertainment is by affected status: families needed an affected sib-pair with atherogenic dyslipidaemia, and the association arm recruited cases with atherogenic dyslipidaemia against normolipidaemic controls, the study being 'initiated in 1999 for the purpose of identifying genes associated with the metabolic syndrome and related traits'.

label: Genomics of Kidney Transplantation
diseases: end stage kidney disease | acute rejection | chronic graft dysfunction | graft failure
quote: Kidney (or kidney-pancreas) transplant recipient no more than 10 days post-transplant, or kidney donor no more than 30 days post-transplant, or previously enrolled in the Genomics of Kidney Transplantation study
note: The recipients are patients transplanted for kidney failure - PMID:30801552 tabulates the 'Cause of End Stage Kidney Disease' of the GEN-03 recipients - and the study follows them for kidney allograft outcomes: 'Aim 1: To identify recipient SNPs that are associated with kidney allograft outcomes, including acute rejection, chronic graft dysfunction, and graft failure.' The kidney donors enrolled beside them are healthy participants, so a curator who counts only the recruitment basis might prefer the role 'at risk' for the allograft outcomes.

label: Génétique de la Néphropathie Diabétique
diseases: insulin-dependent diabetes | proliferative diabetic retinopathy | diabetic nephropathy
quote: As angiotensin II increases glomerular pressure, we studied the relationship between genetic polymorphisms in the renin-angiotensin system-angiotensin I converting enzyme (ACE), angiotensinogen (AGT), and angiotensin II, subtype 1, receptor-and the renal involvement of insulin-dependent diabetic subjects with proliferative retinopathy: those exposed to the risk of nephropathy due to diabetes.
note: Recruitment is by disease: insulin-dependent (type 1) diabetic patients with proliferative retinopathy attending diabetic clinics, graded by the severity of their diabetic nephropathy, the study's subject.

label: GENEVA study
quote: Atopic dermatitis patients were recruited from tertiary dermatology clinics based at three centers (Technische Universität München, as part of the GENEVA study, University of Kiel, University of Bonn) and diagnosed on the basis of skin examination by experienced dermatologists according to standard criteria 31 .
note: A case-control sample whose cases are atopic dermatitis patients recruited at tertiary dermatology clinics; the population controls come from PopGen and KORA.

label: Dental Caries: Whole Genome Association and Gene x Environment Studies
quote: The Dental Caries: GENEVA Genome Wide Association Study (Caries GENEVA Study) is a multi-site collaboration that is part of the GENEVA consortium (www.genevastudy.org).
note: A genome-wide association study of dental caries whose member samples were not recruited on caries status ('Recruiting for all five sample cohorts was not based on participants’ dental caries status', PMID:23259602, for COHRA and the DRDR), so it is a population study of one disease.

label: Genetics of Recurrent Early-Onset Depression
quote: This is a study of a large sample of families with recurrent major depressive disorder (DSM-IV) beginning by the age 30 in probands or 40 in relatives.
